---
$schema: https://poe-platform.github.io/poe-code/schemas/plans/pipeline.schema.json
kind: pipeline
version: 1
readiness: draft
teardown: false
tasks:
  - id: inventory
    title: Establish the complete compatibility inventory
    prompt: |-
      Create a requirement-by-requirement coverage matrix in docs/plans/safe-python.md, using the Python 3.14 language reference, grammar, builtins/types/exceptions reference and the entire standard-library index. Pin the oracle version, build/platform, Unicode version and any imported test/source revisions. For each requirement record implemented-and-verified, partial, missing, blocked or unverified, with source paths, executable evidence and an owning task. Inspect existing code and tests rather than treating old ledger statements as current failures. Include interactive input, annotation/type-parameter semantics, import hooks, runtime introspection and platform/native modules. The user's latest instruction requires no intentional differences and supersedes the historical parse-but-never-evaluate annotation objective. Match CPython annotation and type-parameter behavior exactly, including lazy evaluation and introspection. Missing capabilities are implementation blockers, never exemptions. Do not silently exclude difficult modules or C-backed APIs. Expand this pipeline with bounded per-module/API tasks for every uncovered row before declaring the inventory complete; keep additions in this same file, preserving configured steps and self-contained prompts. This task is the prerequisite for final compliance claims.

      Work in @poe-code/safe-python under packages/safe-python, keeping runtime logic out of the root CLI. Target CPython 3.14.7 and pinned Unicode 16.0.0. Read AGENTS.md and the current implementation before changes; reproduce each suspected gap with a failing test or concrete evidence, and leave already-correct behavior intact. Use TDD for code, fast in-memory unit tests (memfs for filesystem cases), no LLM calls, no host Python/eval as runtime shortcuts, and no ambient host capabilities. Run focused workspace tests, typecheck and scoped ESLint; use npm run build:workspaces -- --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python when a build is needed. Preserve unrelated edits. Record exact evidence and unresolved gaps in docs/plans/safe-python.md. Do not edit README files without user permission; do not commit, push or release as part of these tasks.

      Completion rule: the user requires no intentional differences from CPython 3.14.7 on the pinned reference platform. Preserve sandbox implementation boundaries while implementing the same guest-observable behavior through explicit services. Restricted or unavailable functionality, annotation differences and skipped cases are blockers, not accepted compatibility exceptions. Do not narrow the target to make a task pass.

      No shortcuts: implement complete guest-observable CPython behavior, not an approximation, subset, happy path or test-shaped substitute. No stub modules, dummy return values, silent fallbacks, host-Python subprocess/FFI delegation, host eval, source rewriting to avoid unsupported semantics, test-specific branches, weakened assertions, excluded failures or reduced corpus. Host Python is an external differential oracle only, never the implementation. Mock external services only in fast unit tests; final compatibility evidence must exercise real interpreter components and real supported service adapters. Match values/types, mutation/aliasing, evaluation order, descriptors/introspection, warnings, exceptions and their attributes/tracebacks, import/package behavior, I/O and suspension. Where CPython leaves behavior variable, record its actual contract and verify that contract; do not normalize away meaningful differences. Maintain this same plan until all missing APIs and mismatches are implemented and verified. An unavailable required platform/backend remains unfinished work, never permission to shrink scope.
    status:
      implement: done
  - id: public-runtime
    title: Assemble a usable public interpreter API
    prompt: |-
      Inspect src/index.ts, runtime/module-execution.ts, runtime/runtime-expression-context.ts, runtime/runtime-statement-context.ts, runtime/runtime-values.ts and runtime/runtime-builtins.ts. The package currently exports parsing, analysis and compilation but no assembled execution API. Build a package-owned interpreter/session API wiring existing values, frames, types, builtins, exceptions, compilation and execution; reuse working kernels. Expose typed exec/eval results, namespaces, filename/diagnostics, output/input capabilities, limits and cancellation, with explicit lifetime/isolation rules. All optional capabilities must fail predictably when absent. Prove source-to-result execution using only public imports, with independent sessions, retained session state, guest exceptions and fatal termination. Do not require consumers to reproduce internal test assembly or expose arbitrary JavaScript objects.

  - id: language-audit
    title: Close parser, compiler and scope compliance gaps
    prompt: |-
      Audit existing lexer, parser, analysis and source-program compilation against the pinned full grammar; most syntax and normalized names already exist. Cover valid/invalid syntax, soft keywords, NFKC binding, all source input modes (including interactive/single), byte-source encodings, future flags, comprehensions/walrus, global/nonlocal, class and closure scopes, f/t strings, annotations and type parameters. Use adversarial nesting and diagnostic/source-span cases. Reproduce discrepancies before fixing them and replace the historical never-evaluate-type-expressions policy with exact CPython 3.14 annotation and type-parameter semantics. Acceptance requires a matrix row and executable result for every grammar/scope feature, not reimplementation of passing features.

  - id: annotation-semantics
    title: Replace ignored annotations with exact Python 3.14 semantics
    prompt: |-
      The historical ledger required parsing type syntax without evaluating it. The user has superseded that requirement with no intentional differences. Inspect annotation/type-alias/type-parameter AST, analysis, compilation, runtime-type-parameters.ts and introspection paths; reproduce the current behavior against CPython 3.14.7. Implement the precise evaluation timing, scopes, caching, metadata and errors required for function/class/module annotations, annotated assignments, type aliases, type-parameter bounds/constraints/defaults and future annotations. Include __annotations__, __annotate__ and annotationlib formats, forward references and explicit evaluation APIs. Test deferred side effects, unresolved names, lexical/class scopes, repeated access, mutations and exception timing through public source execution. Never confuse lazy evaluation with never evaluating, or evaluate every annotation eagerly. Use https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/compound_stmts.html#annotations and https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/annotationlib.html plus pinned CPython differential cases as the reference. This task must pass before runtime introspection/library and final compliance tasks can close.

  - id: execution-audit
    title: Complete statement, object and suspension integration
    prompt: |-
      Exercise the public runtime through source programs covering evaluation/callback order, assignments and deletion, closures/defaults/decorators, classes/metaclasses/descriptors/MRO/slots/super, pattern matching, exception chaining/groups and except*, finally/with, yield/yield-from/send/throw/close, coroutines, async generators and async context managers. Inspect runtime/statement-execution.ts, function-invocation.ts and runtime-statement-context.ts: unsupported errors can mean missing capabilities rather than missing kernels. Eliminate reproducible unimplemented paths for supported programs by wiring or fixing the owning component. Verify suspend/resume state, cleanup ordering and fatal cancellation without guest catch/finally suppression. Defer host scheduling authority to explicit capabilities.

  - id: native-types

Cover bytearray/memoryview and buffers, collection views/iterators, generic aliases/unions, code/frame/traceback objects and reflective builtins. Existing string methods are extensively implemented: only change reproduced gaps. Route I/O and import builtins through explicit capabilities owned by their dedicated implementations. No placeholder method may count as implemented; every inventory entry needs behavior evidence.

  - id: single-byte-codecs
    title: Connect ASCII and Latin-1 encoding to the runtime
    prompt: |-
      Inspect runtime/single-byte-encode.ts, runtime/runtime-utf8-encoding.ts, runtime/runtime-string-encode-method.ts and src/unicode-names.ts. The single-byte kernel exists but the default encoder currently only recognizes UTF-8 and an optional fallback. Wire ASCII/Latin-1 aliases through a shared codec abstraction and canonical Unicode-name lookup, without confusing aliases with canonical names. Verify str.encode from public source execution, native subtypes, all supported error modes, adjacent error spans, empty input, unknown handlers, NUL/surrogate names, namereplace, callback ordering and cancellation. Revalidate concurrent Unicode edits without reverting them.

  - id: codec-bytes-construction
    title: Complete bytes construction and codec conversion protocols
    prompt: |-
      Implement the real builtin bytes type and constructor through the native type registry and public PythonSession, preserving the complete CPython 3.14.7 type, subtype, descriptor and buffer contracts. Cover empty/count/iterable/buffer/__bytes__ inputs, __index__ validation, overflow, mutation and aliasing, allocation and cancellation. Connect encoded string construction to the same per-interpreter codec registry and error handlers used by text consumers; verify encoding/errors argument precedence, custom codecs, result subtypes, exceptions and tracebacks. Reproduce the retained constructor batches in session-utf7-shift-boundaries.test.ts (currently NameError for bytes). Replay all constructor and literal rows against the pinned external oracle without replacing guest construction with host-created data. Verify all owned bytes API inventory before closing this row; do not implement a constructor-only stub or literal rewrite. This is a prerequisite of native-types and codec-registry; keep both open until their remaining inventory is verified.

  - id: codec-registry

Test split multibyte input, surrogate policies, negative resume positions, guest failures and cancellation; use the same registry for str/bytes conversions, source decoding and text I/O where Python semantics require it. No host-dependent Unicode/codec behavior may silently change the pinned target.

  - id: codec-unicode-cstring-cache
    title: Share native Unicode UTF-8 caches across codec name consumers
    prompt: >-
      Complete CPython 3.14.7 PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize behavior across native
      codec encoding-name and error-name consumers.
      RuntimeCodecRegistry.unicodeUtf8 now owns per-string identity caches and
      surrogatepass uses registered strict recovery, but
      runtime-codec-registry-functions.ts and other native name binders still
      validate via standalone encodeUtf8 and rebuild the original Unicode
      spelling. Reproduce the recorded cross-consumer probe: cache utf\ud800 as
      utf8 via surrogatepass under a strict handler returning 8, restore strict,
      then codecs.lookup on that same name must return utf-8; it currently
      raises UnicodeEncodeError. Route all affected codec-name boundaries
      through the owning registry cache, preserving exact str/subtype identity,
      failed-conversion retry, reentry, cache lifetime after registry
      invalidation and interpreter isolation. Preserve raw recovered bytes and
      the distinct C-string NUL/length contracts; do not decode arbitrary
      handler-supplied bytes using a host codec or silently coerce them to
      Unicode. Cover lookup, register_error, lookup_error, _unregister_error,
      encode/decode encoding and errors, native kernel errors and str/bytes
      consumers. Verify diagnostic decoding, malformed bytes, custom handler
      return/index validation, callback order, guest failures and cancellation
      with unchanged oracle programs and real supported services. Keep this row
      and codec-registry open until every consumer and their interactions are
      verified.

  - id: codec-callback-recursion
    title: Verify recursive codec callbacks against guest recursion accounting
    prompt: |-
      Own unbounded incremental decoder callback reentry and its interaction with buffered input, native codec frames and recursion accounting. Start with codec-incremental-callback-user-cases.ts and session-codec-incremental-callback-user.test.ts. The initial maxDepth=100 audit differed from the pinned CPython default recursion limit of 1000 and did not isolate a codec bug. With the final fixture maxDepth=1000, all eighteen unbounded buffered decoder reentry cases terminate with reason internal and message Maximum call stack size exceeded instead of completing the caught RecursionError and subsequent reset.     title: Prove indistinguishable behavior with unmodified real Python programs
    prompt: |-
      Validate the assembled interpreter from its public package API with unmodified Python programs and packages, not private helper calls or hand-built substitute runtime contexts. Build a documented corpus covering application-style module trees, package imports, serialization, text/binary files, generators/async execution, decorators/metaclasses, reflection/annotations, numeric/data processing, error handling and representative third-party pure-Python packages with their upstream tests; include required native-backed standard-library and extension workflows through the implemented compatibility mechanisms. Do not mock away imports, native APIs, descriptors, codecs or filesystem semantics under test. ### E3 executable public-session and external-oracle evidence

Execute the following JavaScript at the repository root with `node --import tsx --input-type=module`; execute each identical `source` using `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 -I -c SOURCE` with stdin `hello\n` for the input case. Python is used only as an external oracle. Each case gets a fresh real public session. The error handle is explicitly rendered by guest code; JSON-stringifying opaque guest handles directly is invalid because their primitive getter rejects nonprimitive values.

```javascript
import {PythonSession} from "./packages/safe-python/src/index.ts";
const cases = [
  {
    "name": "public",
    "source": "answer=6*7\nprint(answer)"
  },
  {
    "name": "single",
    "source": "c=compile('1+1', '<probe>', 'single')\nexec(c)"
  },
  {
    "name": "annotation",
    "source": "events=[]\ndef mark(): events.append('evaluated'); return int\ndef f(x:mark())->mark(): pass\nprint(events, callable(f.__annotate__))\nprint(f.__annotations__, events)"
  },
  {
    "name": "alias",
    "source": "events=[]\ndef mark(): events.append('evaluated'); return int\ntype A[T: mark() = int] = list[T]\nprint(events)\nprint(A.__type_params__[0].__bound__, A.__type_params__[0].__default__, A.__value__)"
  },
  {
    "name": "input",
    "source": "print(input('prompt:'))"
  }
];
for (const {name, source} of cases) {
  let output = "";
  const session = new PythonSession({
    limits: {maxSteps: 1000000, maxAllocatedBytes: 16000000, maxDepth: 100},
    hashSeed: [1n, 2n],
    output: {write(text) {output += text;}, flush() {}},
    input: {readLine() {return "hello\n";}}
  });
  const result = session.exec(source);
  if (result.status === "exception") {
    session.globals.set("caught_error", result.exception);
    session.exec("print(type(caught_error).__name__, str(caught_error))");
  }
  console.log(name, result.status, output,
    result.status === "terminated" ? [result.reason, result.message] : []);
}
```

## Evidence and status rules

- **implemented-and-verified**: current real interpreter and supported adapters pass the row's full pinned-oracle contract; record exact corpus and results.
- **partial**: current concrete evidence proves some behavior and identifies an uncovered part.
- **missing**: current executable/source evidence proves the required implementation absent.
- **blocked**: required oracle/backend/dependency prevents implementation or verification; never an exemption.
- **unverified**: no adequate current row-level differential evidence; neither a claim of correctness nor a claim of failure.

**E0** (revalidated 2026-09-12; supersedes the original export inspection): `src/index.ts` exports the assembled `PythonSession` in `src/session.ts`. E3-public passes source-to-result execution. `runtime/runtime-import-statement.ts` implements guest custom import-hook dispatch, but the default session publishes no `__import__`; E3-native reproduces all 297 public module import failures. Each unverified R/G row lists an inspection entry, not proof of implementation ownership or a current failure. Its owner must supply exact implementation/test paths and row-specific evidence. Pending means no adequate API differential has been executed. Historical E1/E2 observations below are retained for provenance, not current failures.

**E1** (executed): the maintained focused workspace command below passed **107 tests in 6 files** (6.98 s, test bodies 236 ms). It covers existing source compilation, type-alias parsing, function definition mechanics, parameter collection, code introspection and annotation-wrapper caching. These are preserved working components; they do not establish complete source-level annotation evaluation or standard-library compliance.

**E2** (historical 2026-09-11 observation; current AST retention and public behavior must use E3): run from the repository root:

```sh
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'JS'
import {compileSourceProgram,parseModule} from './packages/safe-python/src/index.ts';
import {ExecutionBudget} from './packages/safe-python/src/runtime/execution-budget.ts';
try {compileSourceProgram('1+1',{mode:'single',enterRecursiveCall:()=>()=>{}},{string:x=>x,integer:x=>x,tuple:x=>x},new ExecutionBudget({maxSteps:1000000,maxAllocatedBytes:2000000}));} catch(e){console.log(e.name,e.message);}
console.log(JSON.stringify(parseModule('def f(x: missing()) -> missing():\n pass\ntype A[T: missing() = int] = list[T]\n')));
JS
python3 - <<'PY'
import dis
print([x.opname for x in dis.get_instructions(compile('1+1','<string>','single'))])
events=[]
def mark(): events.append('evaluated'); return int
def f(x:mark())->mark(): pass
print(events, callable(f.__annotate__))
print(f.__annotations__, events)
type A[T: mark() = int] = list[T]
print(A.__type_params__[0].__bound__, A.__type_params__[0].__default__, A.__value__)
PY
```

Observed guest compiler: `TypeError unsupported source compilation mode`; CPython accepts single and emits CALL_INTRINSIC_1. The parsed function has parameter name/default but no annotation expressions; type-alias AST retains only kind/name/spans, no value/bounds/default expressions. In CPython, events starts empty and __annotate__ is callable; reading __annotations__ evaluates mark twice and returns int for x/return; the type parameter bound/default are int and alias value is list[T]. Current runtime/statement-execution.ts treats type-alias like pass; runtime/function-definition.ts states type expressions are absent. This is concrete source/AST evidence, not a claimed end-to-end guest differential run.

# Safe Python remaining compliance plan

## Scope and completion criteria

Created 2026-09-11 for the remaining @poe-code/safe-python work. The existing
implementation ledger is preserved verbatim below as historical evidence. Its
earlier pending statements are not a current bug list; inspect current code.

Use CPython 3.14.7 and Unicode 16.0.0, matching the ledger. References:
[language reference](https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/index.html) and
[standard library](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/index.html). The first
task must inventory every requirement and turn broad library families into
bounded executable tasks here. Run tasks in listed order; library tasks require
the public runtime, extension registry and import system, with file-dependent
modules also requiring file objects. Final validation depends on every row.

“Full compliance” requires complete evidence and no intentional differences from
CPython 3.14.7 on the pinned reference platform. The user explicitly rejected
intentional differences. This supersedes the historical objective to never
evaluate annotations: implement exact lazy/eager timing, introspection and type
semantics instead. Sandbox internals must preserve guest-observable behavior
through explicit services. Any missing capability, unsupported module, skipped
case or semantic mismatch blocks completion; no exemptions or narrower target
may be substituted. Historical ledger requirements below do not override this
updated objective.

## No-shortcut acceptance bar

The user requires the full implementation: real Python programs must not need
changes or detect guest-observable differences. There are no accepted intentional
differences. Library-family tasks must be expanded to all required APIs, completed
and checked with unmodified programs; the inventory is not the deliverable for
implementation. Public black-box parity and real-workload validation are mandatory.
No stubs, narrowed subsets, skipped failures, test-only special cases or delegation
of Python execution to host Python are acceptable. No claim of completion while
any required implementation, backend or verification remains missing. The pinned
reference platform makes comparison reproducible; it must not be used to evade
required cross-platform coverage, which the inventory must enumerate explicitly.

- Package metadata is private, depends on safe-fs, and has no README; current

- Existing uncommitted Unicode work is outside this planning edit.

Configured steps come from .poe-code/pipeline/steps.yaml. Implementation tasks
select implement/test; the inventory selects implement. All statuses are open.
The inherited teardown commits all changes, so this draft explicitly disables

## Historical implementation ledger

# Safe Python implementation ledger

## Objective

Build full Python 3 support in a modular, efficient, internally and externally
extensible package. Type syntax must parse and be ignored without evaluating
annotation expressions. Integrate filesystem operations with safe-fs. Commit each
meaningful change. The requested work period is at least five days, with seven
days available; completion also requires evidence of the entire requested scope.

## Initial inspection — 2026-09-08

No safe-python package or project-specific Python specification was found in this
checkout. The initial implementation uses the Python language reference as the
compatibility baseline: https://docs.python.org/3/reference/ . An existing external
specification has been requested from the user. The starting worktree contains
unrelated changes; those are outside this task.

## Implementation and evidence sequence

1. Source positions, newline normalization, lexical tokens, indentation, complete
   Python grammar, and syntax diagnostics. Preserve locations through parsing.
2. Explicit Python values and object protocols, scopes, calls, operators,
   exceptions, control flow, comprehensions, generators, coroutines, classes,
   descriptors, pattern matching, and imports. Do not use host eval or host Python
   as an execution shortcut.
3. Parse annotation and type-parameter syntax, including forward references and
   type aliases, without runtime evaluation of type expressions.
4. Builtins and standard library coverage, with a module-by-module audit and
   explicit capability boundaries for filesystem, processes, network, and native
   extensions. Full compatibility must not imply ambient host authority.
5. safe-fs-backed file objects, imports, paths, filesystem modules, binary/text
   streams, error translation, and cancellation using in-memory tests.
6. Public extension contracts for modules, native callables, and execution
   policy; host objects must not leak unrestricted JavaScript capabilities.
7. Execution limits, cancellation, bounded memory, performance measurements,
   adversarial tests, CPython differential evidence, packaging, and documented
   public options. Expose CLI options through the SDK if a CLI is introduced.

Each stage requires failing tests before code, scoped passing tests and lint,
and a meaningful local commit. Checklists alone do not establish compatibility.
Do not mark the overall goal complete while any language, library, safety,
extension, integration, or validation requirement is missing or unverified.

## Current status

- Implemented source cursor and source diagnostics: universal newlines without
  copying the normalized source, original UTF-16 offsets, Unicode code-point
  columns, initial BOM handling, NUL rejection, stable EOF and lookahead.
- Implemented indentation stack: tab stops, ambiguity detection at equal/greater/
  lesser indentation, form feeds, dedent validation, and EOF flushing. Lexer
  integration is still pending; this does not establish complete lexical support.
- Verified 16 in-memory unit cases after observing missing-module failures before
  implementation. Package typecheck, scoped ESLint, and the maintained selected
  workspace build passed. No CLI visual surface was changed.
- Added a numeric token reader with exact bigint-backed integers, binary/octal/
  hexadecimal bases, decimal floats, imaginary coefficients, underscore grammar,
  leading-zero validation, source spans, and deprecated keyword adjacency warnings.
  It leaves following punctuation for the lexer. Unary signs remain parser work.
- Numeric validation: 99 new unit cases (115 package cases total) pass. An ad hoc
  comparison with CPython 3.14.7 covered 1,380 combinations of integer parts,
  fractional parts, exponents, imaginary suffixes, bases, and malformed separators,
  with no acceptance/value differences. Floating and imaginary values were compared
  by IEEE-754 bytes, including overflow and underflow. This evidence covers literal
  reading only, not numeric operations or the complete lexer.
- Added ordinary/raw string and bytes readers: short/triple quotes, all recognized
  escapes, named Unicode escapes, bytes ASCII restrictions, line continuation,
  normalized newlines, source spans, and first-warning behavior. Text literal
  values are code-point arrays so separate escaped surrogates do not collapse
  into a different Python character. Bytes values use Uint8Array.
- Unicode name lookup uses 45,786 explicit names/aliases and 17 algorithmic
  ranges from pinned Unicode 16.0.0 inputs, matching CPython 3.14.7. It searches
  sorted text without constructing a large lookup map. Generated source includes
  the Unicode license; declaration output is 143 bytes, not a literal-type copy
  of the database. The database is local at runtime; no runtime download or host
  Python dependency is introduced.
- Regenerate the name database with
  `npm run generate:unicode --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`. Input downloads are
  SHA-256 checked in `scripts/generate-unicode.ts`; the pure compilation function

  and `16.0.0/ucd/NameAliases.txt`. Python's omission of algorithmic Tangut names
  and rejection of multi-character named sequences in string escapes are preserved.
- String/Unicode validation: 212 package unit cases pass. CPython comparison
  checked 194,639 canonical-name/alias lookups without differences. A separate

  Focused ESLint, source and generator typechecks, and selected workspace build

- Added Unicode 16 identifier classification and raw name-token reading with
  source spans. Generated/coalesced tables contain 684 start ranges and 800

  The Unicode generator now also hashes and reads `DerivedCoreProperties.txt`.
  No host Unicode character classification or runtime data downloads are used.

  It joins explicit and bracketed physical lines, suppresses comments and blank

  lookup; bound native methods recompute from the current receiver class. Shared
  descriptor/wrapper caches publish successful outer reads and clear nested
  entries when outer initialization fails, matching a reproduced reentrancy case.
  Joining preserves Python code points, including separate surrogate code points.
  Two compiled regressions and one cache-failure regression initially failed;
  six focused tests cover descriptor families, cache sharing, live type identity,
  code points, reentrancy and cancellation. All 105 metadata reads, 30 existing
  metadata cases and 180 native class-method binding/invocation cases match
  CPython. All 6,324 tests in 483 files, selected build, typecheck and scoped lint
  pass. Complete native member/type publication, slot layouts, ModuleType class
  reassignment and full class construction remain unfinished.
- Added live function __defaults__ and __kwdefaults__ reflection, replacement and
  deletion. Lazy containers preserve captured value identity; subsequent calls
  use the replacement tuple or current keyword dictionary. Positional defaults
  align from the right even for overlong tuples. Keyword defaults are looked up
  only for missing keyword-only arguments, after positional validation, matching
  a CPython probe with observable dictionary-key equality. Two compiled cases
  initially failed; additional coverage checks empty containers, lambda defaults,
  deletion, rejected replacement preservation and lazy binding. All 6,329 tests
  in 483 files, selected workspace build, typecheck and scoped lint pass. Full function
  code/closure metadata, canonical native types and class construction remain
  unfinished.
- Added canonical intrinsic descriptor layouts and explicit protocol methods for
  functions and native method/classmethod/wrapper/getset/member descriptors.
  Public __get__, __set__ and __delete__ are actual bound method-wrapper values,
  preserving defining-owner metadata, receiver guards and Python argument-error
  ordering. Explicit gets reuse intrinsic binding without invoking method bodies;
  getsets retain the execution's callback context. Function dictionary shadows
  precede non-data __get__. Native classification remains an execution capability;
  the registry now supplies canonical descriptor types to that capability.
  A compiled function-binding regression initially failed. Three compiled cases
  plus focused family, arity, mutation, cancellation and publication-failure tests
  pass. All 420 explicit protocol cases, 180 existing class-method cases and 105
  qualified-name reads match CPython. All 6,348 tests in 484 files, selected build
  typecheck and scoped lint pass. Complete native type classification/public SDK wiring,
  descriptor metadata catalogs, native constructors and subclass-layout rules
  remain unfinished.
- Added explicit native base-type eligibility, independent of immutability and
  native payload storage. Canonical functions and the five native descriptor
  families reject subclassing; staticmethod/classmethod remain subclassable.
  Allocation checks eligibility before names, namespace processing and class-cell
  publication. The layout constructor repeats the invariant for internal callers,
  including multiple/duplicate bases and attempted subclassable overrides.
  Six regressions initially failed with the wrong namespace-validation error;
  focused coverage also checks publication isolation and allowed native-derived
  hierarchies. All 192 base-eligibility cases, 640 existing class-allocation cases
  and 420 explicit descriptor cases match CPython. All 6,357 tests in 484 files,
  selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass. Complete native constructors,
  slots/layout conflict checks, mutable bases and public execution wiring remain
  unfinished.
- Added shared native storage identity and multiple-base layout validation.
  Heap subclasses/diamonds inherit their native storage root; explicitly extended
  native payloads establish a more-specific identity. Base eligibility and storage
  conflicts are checked in source order before namespace validation/publication.
  Incompatible staticmethod/classmethod/type layouts are rejected, while compatible
  native ancestry and plain mixins remain valid. __class__ compatibility uses the
  same identity, fixing reassignment across an additional native payload layer
  (validated with date/datetime subclass behavior). Two regressions initially
  failed; focused cases cover diamonds, native extensions and error precedence.
  All 432 layout-conflict cases, 238 reassignment cases, 640 allocation cases and
  192 base-eligibility cases match CPython. All 6,361 tests in 484 files, selected
  build, typecheck and scoped lint pass. Heap slot signatures, full solid-base
  sizing/alignment, native constructors and mutable-base invalidation remain
  unfinished.
- Added __slots__ declaration processing and owned slot storage. Declarations
  consume native/guest iterables before validation, preserve source containers,
  validate identifiers without NFKC normalization, mangle/sort names by code point,
  retain duplicate positions and enforce namespace/dictionary/weak-reference and
  variable-sized-base restrictions. Allocation installs member descriptors backed
  by lazy positional storage, independent of dictionaries and wrapper metadata.
  Unset/get/delete behavior, inherited redeclarations, explicit dictionaries and
  empty weak-reference fields now execute through normal descriptor dispatch.
  Storage-bearing heap bases participate in conflict selection; __class__ changes
  compare compatible sibling slot additions without conflating unrelated parents.
  Three allocation regressions initially failed, including reserved __module__
  handling and empty-slotted metaclass dictionaries. Two compiled checks and 18
  focused declaration/storage cases pass. All 608 declaration cases, 256 slotted
  reassignment cases, 238 previous reassignment cases and 192 base-eligibility
  cases match CPython; the 640 allocation and 432 native-layout cases also passed

  scoped lint pass. Actual weak-reference objects/callbacks, slot documentation
  introspection, complete native sizing/alignment, mutable-base invalidation and
  public class-builder/execution wiring remain unfinished.
- Added native __doc__ reflection for descriptor families, bound native methods,
  method wrappers and builtin capabilities. Protocol-wrapper documentation is
  shared by slot; explicit native text (including empty text) is preserved.
  Object/class storage descriptors, subclass hooks and allocation builtins expose
  their documented text. Slot descriptors correctly return None independently of
  dictionary-form __slots__ documentation, which remains available to a future
  inspect.getdoc implementation. Two metadata regressions initially failed;
  seven added tests cover compiled reads, native bindings, overrides, slot docs
  and cancellation. The full suite caught three budget-sensitive regressions
  from a misplaced metadata checkpoint; restricting charges to applicable native
  values fixed them without increasing test budgets. All 50 native documentation
  reads, 105 qualified-name reads and 96 wrapper constructions match CPython.
  All 6,391 tests in 486 files, selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass.
  Complete builtin documentation catalogs, inspect integration, weak-reference
  objects and public class-builder/execution wiring remain unfinished.
- Added native type.__new__ allocation and runtime finalization wiring, enabling
  explicit allocation and ordinary three-argument type calls. Receiver/argument
  validation precedes allocation; unresolved MRO entries are rejected without
  invoking their hook. Metaclass winner selection delegates through ordinary
  __new__ lookup only when necessary, preserving unrelated results and leaving
  metaclass initialization to type calls. Live calling-module metadata, slot
  allocation, set-name/subclass hooks, failure notes and class-cell publication
  use the existing shared mechanisms. Initial compiled construction and long-name
  diagnostic regressions failed before implementation; 13 focused tests cover
  delegation, hook order, conflicts, cancellation and host ownership boundaries.
  All 154 allocator validation cases match CPython. All 6,404 tests in 488 files,
  selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass. Public class-statement builder wiring,
  remaining native constructors, mutable bases and complete execution packaging
  remain unfinished.
- Added native type.__prepare__ as an inherited class-method descriptor. It
  returns independent metered dictionaries without inspecting class arguments or
  mutating keyword inputs. Shared descriptor binding enforces metaclass receivers
  and preserves native metadata. A compiled namespace preparation test initially
  failed with missing __prepare__; four focused tests additionally cover receiver
  precedence, dictionary isolation, binding and cancellation. All 180 binding/call
  cases match CPython. All 6,409 tests in 489 files, selected build, typecheck and
  scoped lint pass. Class-body execution against prepared custom mappings and the concrete

- Added prepared class-body execution through the invocation context. Compiled
  class suites retain defining globals/builtins/closures while using the supplied
  dictionary or custom mapping for locals. Class cells are returned by identity;
  ordinary optimized functions retain their own activation and argument binding.
  Custom mappings use live type-level item slots, preserve names/value identities,
  convert only KeyError lookup/deletion failures, and leave DELETE_NAME's guest
  failure replacement to the frame. Cancellation and host faults cannot become
  missing names. A compiled closure/isolation regression initially failed because
  the execution capability was absent. Eight added tests cover custom mapping
  order, mutation effects, failure boundaries and optimized function behavior.
  All 72 prepared mapping failure traces match CPython. All 6,417 tests in 490
  files, selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass. Concrete __build_class__
  assembly, remaining native constructors and public execution packaging remain
  unfinished.
- Connected the concrete __build_class__ builtin to registry/key policies and
  active invocation capabilities while preserving complete custom contexts.
  Ordinary class statements now resolve replacement bases, select/prepare the
  metaclass, execute prepared bodies, store original bases and validate captured
  class cells through the shared lifecycle. Mapping flags are checked without
  invoking instance attribute overrides; original keyword values reach preparation
  and construction. Integration exposed missing __bases__ reads and native type
  representation; both now support normal metadata access and class-cell errors.
  Native representation preserves code points and follows CPython's simple-name
  fallback for builtins/non-string modules, including a differential-discovered
  regression fixed with failing tests. Eleven added tests cover lifecycle order,
  custom metaclasses, slots, decorators, invalid mappings and cell consistency.
  All 72 concrete builder mapping traces and 80 representation cases match
  CPython; the previous 154 allocator validation and 640 allocation cases also
  match. All 6,428 tests in 491 files, selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass.
  Mutable bases/MRO invalidation, complete native constructors, guest exceptions,
  public execution assembly and packaging remain unfinished.
- Added ordinary guest subscription dispatch for reads, writes, augmented
  assignment and deletion. Live type slots receive original keys and slices;
  class subscriptions prioritize metaclass __getitem__ before ordinary inherited
  __class_getitem__ lookup. Disabled hooks, paired mutation-slot absence and
  unsupported operations retain distinct diagnostics. References resolve receivers
  and keys once but look up slots again at write-back. Prepared custom mappings now
  share the same implementation. Eight added tests cover compiled operations,
  descriptor precedence, key identity, reentrant setter changes and native errors.
  Initial guest assignment and prepared-mapping paired-slot regressions failed.
  Full-suite checks exposed three native tuple write-back regressions, fixed by
  preserving exact-container dispatch without increasing budgets. CPython probes

  All 960 guest subscription cases and 72 concrete builder mapping traces match
  CPython. All 6,436 tests in 491 files, selected build, typecheck and scoped lint pass.
  Native generic aliases, complete constructors, mutable bases/MRO invalidation,
  guest exceptions and public execution assembly remain unfinished.
- Added owned callable-instance dispatch and automatic owned descriptor slots.
  Callability inspects actual-type __call__ presence without binding descriptors;
  invocation ignores instance shadows, binds the live slot and forwards original
  arguments through the shared stack. Instance calls defer keyword-name validation
  until after descriptor binding, preserving disabled-call error precedence.
  Owned __get__/__set__/__delete__ methods now supply ordinary descriptor behavior,
  with paired mutation-slot errors and bounded recursive binding. Explicit
  descriptor extensions retain precedence. Seven added compiled tests cover
  callable/disabled methods, descriptor effects, data precedence and stack recovery.
  Initial instance-call, custom-descriptor and keyword-order regressions failed

  complete native constructors, mutable bases and public execution assembly remain

- Added live call/get/data-descriptor dispatch for staticmethod/classmethod heap

  Classmethod subclasses reflect their own call-slot presence. Explicit native

- Added custom call-keyword mapping expansion through ordinary keys lookup and

- Connected dictionary display unpacking to shared guest mapping merges through

  Six added cases cover overwrite order, live numeric keys, descriptor lookup,

  update-method invocation still needs its active capability forwarded; full

- Connected fromkeys to active guest iteration and exposed the native capability

- Connected dictionary-item view disjointness, intersection and item-view xor

- Added automatic __hash__ = None to class namespaces defining __eq__ without

- Added an execution hash-slot adapter and connected hash() to active guest
  methods, including nested immutable members. Explicit extension hash policies

  Collection key-policy assembly still needs to
  adopt the same adapter; canonical object.__hash__, native type catalogs and

- Corrected the hash descriptor lookup error boundary: AttributeError raised
  while binding __hash__ means unhashable, but AttributeError from the invoked

  The initial regression leaked the binding AttributeError. Four added cases

- Added a reusable execution-owned collection key-policy factory composing the

  Selected workspace build, typecheck, scoped lint and all 6,534 tests in 492
  files pass (two workers).
- Added call-stack-aware execution key storage and frame binding in concrete
  program assembly. Registry/bootstrap storage and guest collections can now

  Four new tests cover these paths, nested frame restoration, exception cleanup,

- Installed canonical object.__hash__ as a native wrapper descriptor, including

  Ten added tests cover direct/bound/inherited calls, explicit hash restoration

- Installed native object.__ne__ with a receiver-only comparison capability.

- Installed canonical object.__eq__ with identity-or-NotImplemented semantics.

- Core match execution (2026-09-11): three failing native statement tests

- Lexical depth limits and expression recursion policy (2026-09-11): ten failing
  tests reproduced acceptance of excessive delimiter/indentation/interpolation
  nesting, including a host RangeError on 10,000 parentheses. The lexer now
  enforces CPython's 200 delimiter levels, 100 indentation-stack entries
  (including the base level) and 150 interpolation-mode entries (including
  ordinary mode). Replacement-field braces participate in total delimiter depth;
  literal and field counters are restored as modes close. Excess indentation
  does not grow state and is attributed to the physical line start. Excess
  f/t-string nesting is attributed to the final opening quote, including triple
  quotes. An older test accepting 300 nested f-strings contradicted both CPython
  compile and tokenize; it now covers the valid 149-level boundary and rejection
  of the next level. Five additional failing tests reproduced host-stack errors
  from recursive unary, power and lambda grammar and absent recursion ownership.
  LexerOptions/TokenCursor now carry an optional host-owned enterRecursiveCall
  policy; expression parsing restores each successful entry in a finally block.
  Tests stop 10,000-level inputs at a configured depth and verify restoration
  after success and syntax/resource errors. This does not impose a new arbitrary

## Public session assembly audit — 2026-09-11

Status: **unfinished against the required CPython completion rule**. The package now
has an assembled execution entry point, but this does not complete the interpreter
or permit compatibility exceptions. The five concrete differential mismatches below
remain blockers in this same plan. No commit, push, release or README edit.

### Implemented API and lifetime

- `src/index.ts` exports `PythonSession` and typed options, exec/eval result unions,
  guest handles, namespaces, syntax diagnostics, warnings and unraisable reports.
  `src/session.ts` owns values, SipHash policy, type and exception registries,
  builtin registration, dictionaries, call frames, compilation/code identity,
  execution and the cumulative execution budget. No root CLI runtime was added.
- `exec(source, options)` returns `ok`, `exception`, `diagnostic` or `terminated`;
  `eval` additionally returns a guest handle on success. Source accepts text or
  bytes; run options include filename, optimization, globals and locals. Guest
  exceptions retain their guest object and mutations; syntax diagnostics preserve
  the compiler's filename, positions and source line. The exception result's
  filename identifies the submitted call, not a reconstructed traceback.
- Default globals persist. `createNamespace()` creates another owned dictionary;
  separate globals/locals can be selected per call. Dynamic `compile`, `eval`,
  `exec`, `globals` and `locals` use the existing code and dictionary kernels.
  Functions retain their defining namespaces across calls. Sessions own separate
  registries, builtins, identities, exception state and namespace dictionaries.
- `value` admits only null, boolean, bigint, number and string. Guest handles
  expose a storage-kind tag and primitive projection, never internal mutable
  JavaScript objects. Nonprimitive projection, forged handles and cross-session
  handles/namespaces are rejected. `globals.get/set/delete/names` and the same
  methods on created namespaces provide controlled access; `names` returns string
  binding names. No arbitrary host callable injection is exposed.
- Limits and a two-word unsigned 64-bit hash seed are required. Supply an
  unpredictable seed for untrusted code; runtime initialization never discovers
  ambient randomness. Steps and charged allocation accumulate across startup,
  compilation, execution and metered bridge operations. These are cooperative
  accounting limits, not a proven complete heap/CPU bound. Cancellation uses an
  explicit AbortSignal and synchronous checkpoints; execution does not yield the
  event loop. A fatal execution result is latched for subsequent exec/eval calls.
  Call-depth exhaustion uses the existing guest RecursionError policy.
- Synchronous output (`write`, `flush`), input (`readLine`: decoded line including
  its ending, or null for EOF), warning and unraisable sinks are explicit optional
  services. Installed input/output methods are bound and snapshotted. Print keeps
  incremental writes and supports guest file objects through guest attribute/call
  dispatch. Input converts prompts with guest protocols, flushes, reads, removes
  one trailing LF and raises native EOFError at EOF. The internal native-error
  type now admits EOFError for existing exception normalization.
- Missing services fail explicitly, including missing unraisable reporting;
  asynchronous service results are rejected instead of returning premature
  success. Service cancellation is checked even on failure. No filesystem,
  network, process, console or input service is selected implicitly. Reentrant
  session calls from service callbacks are rejected. Callback report handles may
  be retained and inspected after execution returns.
- `close()` is idempotent, invalidates handle/namespace operations and subsequent
  execution, and performs no metered cleanup or guest finalizers. It remains
  callable after cancellation. Drop session and handle references for host GC;
  deterministic guest finalization is still unfinished. Constructor validation
  and initialization may throw before a session exists. Invalid host API usage
  throws; the result union describes submitted execution.

- `src/session.test.ts` has 14 passing in-memory tests importing only the public

- The step-limit test reserves sufficient allocation budget so that it exercises

function scopes. Errors identify the entire offending comprehension, excluding
extra grouping parentheses. Yield validation now retains the owning
comprehension kind and reports its content span. Traversals retain metering.

#### Reproduced gaps and implemented changes

- The AST discarded parameter/return/assignment annotations, alias values, and
  type-parameter expressions. Two new retention tests failed before changes.
  ASTs now retain those expressions, including starred annotations/defaults,
  normalized and spelled parameter names, kinds, bounds/constraint tuples,
  defaults and source spans. The parser reader is now `readTypeParameters`.
  Existing grammar checks and execution-budget tests remain active. Historical
  parser assertions requiring discarded fields were replaced with retention
  assertions; this does not establish runtime evaluation of those fields.
- Three initial public-source custom-annotator tests failed because assigning
  `f.__annotate__` terminated with `capability: runtime operation has no installed
  capability`. Function state now stores the annotator independently of the
  annotation cache. Ordinary guest calls supply integer format `1` on an
  uncached `__annotations__` read; successful dictionaries (including subclasses)
  are retained by identity. Failures do not manufacture a cache.
- Callable assignment invalidates the cache, including assignment of the same
  callable. Assigning `None` to `__annotate__` preserves an existing cache.
  Setting/deleting `__annotations__` disables its annotator. Invalid setters
  preserve state and raise the CPython error messages. Nested successful writes
  are replaced by the outer successful evaluation; nested writes survive an
  exception. Direct calls to a custom `__annotate__` do not use the owner's cache.
- Callability is checked without invoking descriptors, and checked again when
  reading annotations after mutation of the callable object's type. The pinned
  oracle returns `{}` if its call slot has disappeared. A new failing regression
  reproduced this gap before the second callability check was added. Invalid
  return values raise `__annotate__ returned non-dict of type '...'`, with the
  existing UTF-8 diagnostic truncation policy at CPython's 100-byte limit.
- Public-source annotation syntax tests failed before changes: direct named
  expressions executed successfully in ordinary annotations; the future-import
  variant reached an unavailable runtime import instead of a compilation error.
  Annotation expressions now receive their own non-async expression validation,
  including local and non-simple assignment annotations and future annotations.
  Direct named/yield/await expressions are rejected; nested lambda/generator
  scopes and comprehension binding rules remain separate.

Pinned timing observation for compiler-generated annotations (still a blocker):
`events=[]; def mark(): events.append('called'); return int`, followed by
`def f(x:mark())->Missing:pass`, leaves `events == []`. Two failed reads of
`f.__annotations__` each raise `NameError: name 'Missing' is not defined` and
append once. After `Missing=str`, the next read yields
`{'x': int, 'return': str}` and appends once. Repeated reads return that same
cached dictionary without appending. `f.__annotate__(1)` appends again.
The implemented custom-callable protocol has corresponding public-source tests;
the compiler does **not yet generate that callable** from retained annotations.

| Explicit global before unreachable alias, and class lookup before conditional unreachable alias | Both read global `42` | Already correct | Preserved |

### 2026-09-11 public runtime control-flow continuation: native super integration

Status: **unfinished against the unchanged CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0
completion rule**. This continuation fixes a reproduced missing public runtime

compatibility or waive any prior annotation, library, platform, service, traceback,

Read the root AGENTS.md and current statement-execution.ts,
function-invocation.ts, runtime-statement-context.ts, runtime-program.ts,
RuntimeExceptionExecution, GeneratorExecution, session assembly, type registry,
and descriptor/super lookup components before editing. The inspected runtime

hooks in generic components are not by themselves evidence of a public gap.
No existing correct control-flow behavior was changed.

#### Reproduced failure and owning-component fix

Added `src/runtime-source-control.test.ts` with eight public PythonSession source
programs. Initial run: **7 passed, 1 failed**. The class/metaclass/MRO/slots program
raised `NameError: name 'super' is not defined`. The class body called
`super().__new__(m,n,b,d)` from its metaclass and `super().f()` from a subclass.
The existing super-attributes.ts supplied descriptor/MRO lookup, but there was no
native super type or public builtin installation.

Added runtime-super.ts to own native proxy storage, allocation, initialization,
zero-argument activation lookup, explicit type/instance validation, unbound and
bound descriptor behavior, subtype rebinding, native members, representation and
documentation. It calls the existing readSuperAttribute and
resolveRuntimeClassAttribute kernels. The type registry publishes its canonical
native type; PythonSession installs that type. Runtime invocation explicitly
supplies the calling optimized frame for zero-argument super. There is no host
stack inspection, ambient authority, host scheduler, Python delegation, guest
source rewriting, eval shortcut, or root CLI logic.

Two further red/green checks caught defects during this implementation:
`super(A).__get__(None)` and `super(A).__get__(None,None)` must raise
`TypeError: __get__(None, None) is invalid`; both initially returned the proxy.
A metadata test initially failed because the native type/member documentation
was not installed. All these failures were fixed without deleting or weakening
the assertions. An initial typecheck found two optional local-value types in
argument resolution; explicit union annotations fixed those errors.

#### Source-program evidence

The worktree test corpus contains **23 tests**, with no skipped or
excluded tests. It uses real compiler/interpreter components and in-memory guest
state. It does not create filesystem fixtures or call an LLM. Its 22 ordinary
Python cases were also executed unchanged against the built dist/index.js public
entry and the external oracle; all source/assertion pairs passed on both.

| Source-program area | Observations asserted |
| --- | --- |
| Callback/assignment/deletion order | RHS callback before target-key callback, then __setitem__; deletion-key callback before __delitem__ |
| Closures/defaults/decorators | Decorator expressions top-down, applications bottom-up, default captures old value while closure sees mutation |
| Classes/metaclasses/slots/super | Metaclass allocation through super, method MRO lookup, slot storage, no unexpected instance dictionary |
| Pattern matching | Failed guard retains captures; subsequent case observes correct subject and bindings |
| Exception cleanup | Context entry, raising through try/except with explicit cause, finally before __exit__, suppression by __exit__ |
| Generator delegation | yield-from forwards send/throw, yields expected values, close runs child cleanup before parent cleanup |
| Coroutine/async context manager | __aenter__ and __aexit__ suspend; sent values and return value survive resume |
| Async generator | __anext__ result and aclose awaiting finally cleanup |
| super validation | Eleven exact type/message checks: missing arguments, invalid anchor/receiver, keywords, arity, invalid None descriptor binding, deleted arg0 and missing class cell |
| super descriptors | Instance/class binding, descriptor owner/instance identity, reported __class__, native member identities, fresh/unbound proxy state |
| super subtype/reinitialization | Subclass constructor runs on rebinding, already-bound descriptor remains unchanged, failed initialization retains prior binding, cell-backed arg0 works |
| super metadata | Read-only members, type/member documentation |
| Fatal cancellation | Explicit output adapter aborts after writing `cancel`; output is exactly `["cancel"]`, with no guest except/finally/__exit__ output; session remains terminated |

- `ExceptionGroup("x",[ValueError("y")])` raises

  executes the subsequent body, and runs finally.
- Failed destructuring of a with target exits the entered manager; suppression
  skips the body and acquisition of the next manager.
- Finally continue overrides pending break and preserves loop-else behavior.
- Generator close returns a finalizer return value once; repeated close returns None.
- Yielding while handling GeneratorExit rejects close and retains suspension;
  a subsequent close runs cleanup once.
- A suspended except handler retains its exception for bare raise and deletes
  the exception alias on completion.
- With suppression inside finally preserves the earlier pending return.
- Yield-from receives the child return value when throw is handled by the child.
- Context-manager exit failure preserves the body's exception as __context__.

Two further source tests use an explicitly supplied output service that aborts
the execution signal on its first write. Cancellation during coroutine async
exit and during async-generator awaited cleanup terminates immediately, emits
only `cancel`, bypasses guest catch/finally, and prevents subsequent execution.
These are sandbox cancellation assertions, not CPython host-cancellation claims.
No scheduling authority or ambient host services were introduced.

An initial test expectation that delegate close raising StopIteration must
produce RuntimeError was disproved by the pinned oracle. The expectation was
corrected before retaining the regression. No production change was made for
this already-correct behavior. The final test also asserts continuation with
value 9, distinguishing delegation completion from silently dropping the error.

#### Revalidated blockers

Built public PythonSession still reports:

- `ExceptionGroup("x",[ValueError("y")])`: guest exception,
  `name 'ExceptionGroup' is not defined`.
- `try:\n raise ValueError("y")\nexcept* ValueError:\n pass\n`:
  `{status:'terminated', reason:'internal', message:'unsupported statement: try'}`.
  The owning statement machine explicitly rejects `statement.group`.

These are required missing capabilities, not accepted restrictions. Complete
exception-group construction, matching, split/merge/reraise semantics,
attributes/tracebacks and suspension remain unfinished. Existing annotation,
platform/service and broader corpus blockers remain open. This pass did not
implement those APIs or verify all edge cases, and did not reduce the target.

- Full maintained workspace unit route:
  `npm run test:unit --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`: **631 files, 9,723 tests
  passed**, 29.45 seconds, no skips/exclusions.
- Strengthened the delegate continuation assertion after that full run; final
  focused rerun of `src/runtime-cleanup-edge.test.ts`: **11/11 passed**.
- `npm run typecheck --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`: passed.
- Scoped ESLint on the new test file: passed.
- `npm run build:workspaces -- --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`: passed,
  maintained safe-fs/safe-python build closure.
- Final built public entry versus external oracle: **9/9 source/assertion pairs**.
- No runtime implementation changes, README changes, commits, pushes or releases.
  No visual CLI behavior changed; screenshot validation does not apply.


### 2026-09-11 builtin surface inventory and reproduced runtime gaps
Status: **unfinished**. The target remains CPython 3.14.7 on the pinned
platform with Unicode 16.0.0, with no intentional differences. This inventory
records observations, not an implementation-completeness claim. Publication or
a matching descriptor kind does **not** count as behavior implementation.
Every row marked unverified below remains an acceptance blocker; existing tests
must still be traced to individual contracts and expanded where insufficient.
No placeholder is counted as implemented.

#### Reference and scope

- External oracle: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`.
- Version: `3.14.7 (main, Aug  5 2026, 10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`.
- Platform: `macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O`; Unicode `16.0.0`.
- Source: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/bltinmodule.c>,
  specifically `builtin_input_impl`, `builtin_vars`, and builtin publication.
- Namespace includes normal site initialization (`help`, `quit`, `exit`,
  `copyright`, `credits`, `license`), metadata and private exception names.
  No `-S` exclusion was applied.
- Enumerated all 159 entries in this oracle's `vars(builtins)`, and 156 type
  expressions comprising builtin exception/type names, types exported by
  `types`, types of builtin namespace objects, native descriptors, collection
  views and iterators, generic aliases/unions and execution objects. The 5,508
  effective member rows include inherited members with their reference owner.
  Additional types reachable only through missing modules/native backends remain
  discovery work; this is not a claim that all interpreter/stdlib types are closed.

#### Reproduction and implementation evidence

1. `src/session-input-compatibility.test.ts`: initial focused run **1 failed,
   7 passed**. For `readLine() => ""`, the guest retained the sentinel
   `message='no exception'`; the oracle with `sys.stdin=io.StringIO('')` raised
   `EOFError('EOF when reading a line')`. Implemented empty-line EOF in
   `src/runtime/builtin-input.ts`, moved input argument validation, prompt
   conversion and line handling out of `src/session.ts`, and retained explicit
   service ownership in the session adapter. Neighbor cases `\n`, `\r\n`,
   `a\r\n`, `a\r`, `a` already matched and were preserved. `null` remains
   the explicit service EOF marker. Focused input/session run: **22 passed**.
2. `src/session-vars.test.ts`: initial run **10 failed**, including guest
   `NameError` instead of `vars` execution. Added `src/runtime/builtin-vars.ts`
   and publication through `src/runtime/runtime-code-builtins.ts`. Tests cover
   module identity/mutation, independent optimized-frame snapshots, instance
   dictionary identity, class mappingproxy, one full attribute lookup returning
   arbitrary values, keyword-before-arity errors, conversion of AttributeError
   and preservation of ValueError. Focused vars/code-builtins run: **18 passed**.
   A draft error test used `__getattr__` on an instance that already had a dict;
   it was corrected to `__getattribute__` before relying on that expectation.
   External CPython and built public entry each passed the same **12 source/
   assertion pairs** listed below.
3. `src/session-async-generator-member.test.ts`: initial run **1 failed**,
   `getset_descriptor` versus oracle `member_descriptor` for `ag_running`.
   Changed only its descriptor constructor in
   `src/runtime/runtime-async-generator-descriptors.ts`. The underlying live
   activity payload is unchanged. The new test checks descriptor kind, class
   binding identity, None doc, readonly assignment/deletion, invalid receiver
   diagnostics, true while awaiting and false after yielding. Focused new test,
   type integration and member descriptor tests: **1,195 passed**.

No root CLI code, README, commit, push or release is part of this work. Existing
string methods were left intact. Filesystem/LLM services are not called by unit
tests. The external Python executable was used only for reference observations,
not by runtime code or unit tests.

#### Remaining compatibility blockers

- Missing canonical publication is detailed per row, including exception groups,
  OSError family/aliases, MemoryError, bytes/bytearray/memoryview/property,
  `dir`, `open`, `__import__`, `breakpoint`, site helpers and module metadata.
- `enumerate`, `filter`, `map`, `reversed`, `zip` remain functions instead of
  canonical type objects. Calling a working iterator kernel does not close
  construction, descriptor, subtype, introspection or type identity contracts.
- `runtime-type-registry.ts::nativeType` still has no canonical iterator or
  buffer type path. The inventory records fatal capability results for these;
  it does not treat them as expected compatibility behavior.
- Input still lacks complete sys stream replacement, stderr flushing, TTY/
  readline, audit hooks, and guest flush-error behavior. `InputContext` describes
  the existing noninteractive text-service path; it is not a restricted target.
  Real supported full I/O/import service adapters and their differential corpus
  are unfinished. Unit callback evidence is not final backend compatibility.
- Every published member still needs per-contract behavior evidence covering
  binding/keywords, base-descriptor versus override dispatch, subtype payloads,
  aliasing/mutation, evaluation order, exception attributes/tracebacks and error
  precedence. Do not infer these from the descriptor-kind column.
- Generic alias/union, code/frame/traceback, buffers/views and iterators have
  explicit rows but their full behavior corpus remains unfinished.
- Oracle temporary async-generator asend/athrow objects emitted unawaited
  RuntimeWarnings during enumeration. Warning/finalization parity is not
  established by this metadata scan and remains a blocker.

#### How to reproduce the publication observations

Use a freshly built `PythonSession` from `packages/safe-python/dist/index.js`,
limits `{maxSteps:100000000,maxAllocatedBytes:500000000,maxDepth:200}` and
`hashSeed:[1n,2n]`. No host execution delegation is configured.

For each builtin row evaluate `type(__builtins__[NAME]).__name__`, where NAME is
that row's quoted literal. A missing entry raises KeyError because this probe
uses the builtin namespace dictionary; ordinary name lookup raises NameError.
This column measures namespace lookup and concrete runtime type, not callable
semantics or metadata content.

For each type section use a fresh session and the following setup (all 156
setups succeeded), then evaluate `EXPRESSION.__name__` and assign
`inventory_type=EXPRESSION`. For each member use its owner's index in the
reference MRO below and evaluate
`type(inventory_type.__mro__[INDEX].__dict__[NAME]).__name__`.
A missing owner blocks its dependent member probes; those rows are explicitly
marked `owner unavailable`, not represented as executed member behavior tests.
A matching kind still has status **behavior unverified**. This also means that
an unexpected MRO must be investigated rather than hiding it by normalizing the
index. Guest errors were inspected through their guest class names; termination
messages are retained verbatim in the table.

```python
def f(): return None
class C:
 def f(self): pass
 def __getitem__(self,i): raise IndexError

def closure():
 x=1
 def inner(): return x
 return inner

async def ac(): pass
async def ag(): yield 1
coro=ac()
agen=ag()
try: 1/0
except BaseException as e: tb=e.__traceback__
```

Publication owners inspected: `src/runtime/runtime-builtins.ts`,
`src/runtime/runtime-type-registry.ts`, `src/runtime/runtime-code-builtins.ts`,
`src/runtime/runtime-native-attribute.ts`, `src/session.ts`,
`src/runtime/standard-exception-catalog.ts`, native descriptor implementations
including `runtime-async-generator-descriptors.ts`,
`runtime-exception-argument-member.ts`, `runtime-getset-descriptor.ts`, and
`runtime-member-descriptor.test.ts`. These paths are relative to
`packages/safe-python`. Source presence alone is not verification.

#### Built public vars differential assertions

Each setup runs in a fresh namespace/session; the assertion must evaluate to the
actual boolean True on both the oracle and the built guest. These use real
interpreter components and require no external service.

Case 1:

```python

assert vars() is globals()
```

Case 2:

```python
vars()['answer']=42
assert answer==42
```

Case 3:

```python
def f():
 x=1
 first=vars()
 first['x']=99
 second=vars()
 return x==1 and second['x']==1 and first is not second
assert f()
```

Case 4:

```python
class C: pass
c=C()
vars(c)['answer']=42
assert vars(c) is c.__dict__ and c.answer==42
```

Case 5:

```python
class C: pass
assert type(vars(C)).__name__=='mappingproxy'
```

Case 6:

```python
events=[]
class C:
 def __getattribute__(self,name):
  events.append(name)
  return 42
c=C()
value=vars(c)
assert value==42 and events==['__dict__']
```

Case 7:

```python
try: vars(1)
except TypeError as e: message=e.args[0]
assert message=='vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute'
```

Case 8:

```python
try: vars(1,2)
except TypeError as e: message=e.args[0]
assert message=='vars expected at most 1 argument, got 2'
```

Case 9:

```python
try: vars(1,2,x=3)
except TypeError as e: message=e.args[0]
assert message=='vars() takes no keyword arguments'
```

Case 10:

```python
try: vars(x=3)
except TypeError as e: message=e.args[0]
assert message=='vars() takes no keyword arguments'
```

Case 11:

```python
class C:
 def __getattribute__(self,name):raise AttributeError('lookup')
try:vars(C())
except Exception as e: result=(e.__class__.__name__,e.args[0])
assert result==('TypeError','vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')
```

Case 12:

```python
class C:
 def __getattribute__(self,name):raise ValueError('lookup')
try:vars(C())
except Exception as e: result=(e.__class__.__name__,e.args[0])
assert result==('ValueError','lookup')
```

overrides in the test remain uncalled, verified by an empty event list.

rows, not canonical type publication or their complete member surfaces.

### 2026-09-11 — Registry dispatch, factory construction and text-codec checks

Status: **partial and unfinished**. `codec-registry` is not closed; no encoding
family or public module/API row is marked verified by this work. The existing
registry kernel and its tests were already present in the dirty workspace.

Implemented in `packages/safe-python/src/runtime/runtime-codec-registry.ts`:

- General encode/decode dispatch invokes the selected native tuple slot with the
  original source, distinguishes omitted errors from an explicit empty errors
  string, validates the result's native two-tuple shape including tuple subtypes,
  preserves output identity, and deliberately does not inspect the consumed-count
  entry. Encoding/error arguments validate their C-string boundaries in order.
- Callback failures retain exception identity and append CPython's operation and
  original-encoding note through the existing interpreter exception protocol.
  Lookup, result-shape, incremental factory and stream factory errors do not gain
  that note. Host failures and fatal cancellation are not guest codec failures.
- Text lookup bypasses metadata for exact tuples, otherwise reads live
  `_is_text_encoding` on every request even when the CodecInfo is cached. It
  suppresses only AttributeError, uses guest truth conversion, and matches the
  precision-limited nontext diagnostic with complete UTF-8 characters.
- Incremental encoder/decoder construction resolves the factory through ordinary
  guest attribute access. Stream reader/writer construction selects the matching
  tuple slot and preserves guest stream identity. These are factory dispatch
  operations, **not** a claim that native incremental/stream classes are installed.
- Unregister checks cancellation even when the search path is empty. Existing
  registration identity, successful-hit caching, search-path mutation and custom
  error-handler position semantics remain intact.

### 2026-09-11 — UTF-8 signature kernels and text-conversion integration

Status: **unfinished**. This advances `codec-utf8-bom`; it does not close that
child, `codec-unicode-transforms`, or `codec-registry`. The existing bounded
family tasks remain in this pipeline. Registry test status was `done` when
inspected despite the missing public APIs; changed it to `open` using the YAML

Reference and reproduction:

- External differential oracle: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython 3.14.7
  built August 5, 2026 with Clang 21.0.0; macOS 26.4.1 arm64, little endian,
  Unicode 16.0.0. Inspected its actual `encodings.utf_8_sig` module and
  <https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/codecs.html#encodings.utf_8_sig>.
  Python was used only outside the implementation as an oracle.
- Four public `PythonSession` tests initially failed: empty UTF-8 signature
  encoding, normalized encoding spelling, surrogatepass encoding, and lazy
  unknown-handler lookup. All returned guest exception status instead of `ok`.
- New kernel tests initially failed to load because the signature kernel was
  absent. A subsequent text-decoder regression failed with exact
  `LookupError: unknown encoding: UTF 8 SIG` before decoder integration.
- Corrected the new test's table representation after Vitest expanded byte
  arrays into positional arguments. The intended partial-BOM assertions were
  retained, and empty/one-/two-byte cases all execute.

Implementation and verified behavior:

- Added `src/runtime/utf8-signature.ts` with stateless encoding/decoding and
  incremental encoder/decoder state kernels over the existing UTF-8 kernels.
  The BOM is immutable package-owned data; no host text codec or Unicode
  conversion determines results.
- Stateless encoding emits a BOM even for empty input. Decoding strips only
  the first leading BOM and counts its bytes as consumed. Decode errors refer
  to the post-BOM input and UTF-8 offsets/encoding, matching the oracle.
- Incremental decoding buffers partial BOMs even with `final=True`. Recognition
  changes initial state before a later Unicode failure while keeping the old
  byte buffer. Encoding likewise consumes initial state before a Unicode error.
  Integer state is preserved without Boolean normalization; reset, buffer
  ownership, mutable error policy, strict failure recovery, allocation failure,
  and cancellation checkpoints are covered.
- Added signature dispatch to the existing native text encoder/decoder adapters.
  Public `str.encode` and `str(bytes, encoding, errors)` use these real components.
  Existing fallback hooks, unknown-handler laziness and UTF-8 behavior remain.
  These adapters are still not the interpreter-owned registry; shared registry
  integration remains required and is not claimed by this change.
- Ten assertions in `src/session-utf8-signature.test.ts` passed both in the real
  interpreter and independently in the pinned oracle. They cover returned
  bytes/strings and exact Unicode error encoding/object/start/end/reason.
- All 90 chunk-boundary/error-policy combinations for BOM + ASCII + euro sign +
  supplementary scalar + embedded BOM passed in the kernels and oracle. Separate
  oracle assertions confirmed partial final BOMs, failure-state transitions,
  negative integer state restoration, error-policy recovery, and byte-at-a-time
  surrogatepass/surrogateescape roundtrips.
