### 2026-09-11 — Standard codec handlers, native mutation and public integration inventory

Status: **unfinished**. `codec-registry` and `codec-registry-integration` remain
open. Reopened both `codec-registry` YAML status scalars (`implement`, `test`)
that still said `done`; the historical kernel results do not close this parent.
No public codec module/API row below is claimed implemented-and-verified.
All sibling codec-family tasks remain required. This entry neither reduces the
CPython target nor accepts unavailable functionality as a compatibility exception.

Implemented in this work:

- `src/runtime/runtime-codec-errors.ts` supplies interpreter-owned callable
  objects for `strict`, `ignore`, `replace`, `xmlcharrefreplace`,
  `backslashreplace`, `namereplace`, `surrogateescape`, and `surrogatepass`.
  Each registry owns distinct objects; lookup identity is stable within one
  registry; replacing a registration does not replace another interpreter's
  object. Native docs, names, qualified names, null module/self and positional-only
  text signatures are published through the native callable metadata protocol.
- Handlers use internal Unicode exception storage and the actual exception MRO,
  bypassing guest field descriptors and `__getattribute__`. They clamp error
  ranges without rewriting exception fields or args. Strict and surrogate
  rejection preserve the original exception instance. Wrong-type diagnostics
  use native qualified type metadata. Unicode names use package-owned Unicode
  16.0.0 tables, including algorithmic names and unnamed-code-point escapes.
- Surrogateescape limits one decode replacement to four non-ASCII bytes.
  Surrogatepass has the C handler's own spelling recognizer (not codec registry
  normalization): ASCII-case-insensitive UTF spellings, case-sensitive
  `cp65001`, C-string NUL termination, and pinned little-endian UTF-16/32.
  Decoder consumption can exceed the reported error end to consume one encoded
  surrogate. It validates encoding before the object, as CPython does.
- `RuntimeCodecRegistry.unregisterError` returns whether a custom registration
  existed and protects all eight builtin names even after their handlers have
  been replaced. Registry search/cache behavior was left intact.
- `handleError` rereads native `UnicodeDecodeError.object` **after** tuple and
  integer-index validation, returns its identity, and applies bounds against
  its current length. `__index__` can mutate that object. Encoding retains the
  caller's original length. Existing generic kernel callbacks that are not
  Unicode decode exceptions retain their previous contract.
- `namereplace` uses the clipped start as the resume position for inverted
  ranges; other replacement handlers retain their own different end contract.
  An 804-case differential run found this mismatch and a failing regression
  preceded the correction.

Reference and evidence:

- External differential oracle only: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`,
  `3.14.7 (main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0
  (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`, `sys.platform == 'darwin'`, Unicode **16.0.0**.
  No Python, host text codec, host Unicode table, eval or FFI is used by runtime
  implementation. No new ambient service was introduced.
- Read the exact v3.14.7 reference implementations:

  [Objects/exceptions.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/exceptions.c),

  and the pinned installation's `Lib/codecs.py` and encoding modules.

### 2026-09-11 — UTF-16/32 kernels and registry-backed recovery

Status: **unfinished**. Component evidence for `codec-utf16-32` does not close
that row or `codec-registry`. Public modules, streams and consumers remain
required. No compatibility exception was accepted or family row closed.

Implemented under packages/safe-python/src/runtime:

- `utf-wide.ts`: UTF-16/32 encoding and ex-decode in both explicit byte orders
  and pinned native little-endian order, using explicit byte arithmetic. Covers
  BOM emission/detection, consumed counts, partial units, surrogate pairs,
  invalid UTF-32 scalars, standard error policies and exact native error fields.
  No host TextDecoder, Unicode table, Python delegation, eval or ambient service.
- `utf-wide-incremental.ts`: owned buffers, integer state, reset/restoration,
  missing-BOM errors and state after failure. Native encoders retain initial
  state after failure, unlike UTF-8-signature. Every byte split of multibyte
  text is tested in both orders, including native detection of big-endian BOMs.
- `runtime-codec-recovery.ts`: a per-operation bridge to the interpreter registry,
  lazily caching the handler and native guest exception. Re-registration affects
  the next operation. Reuses registry return/position validation, including
  negative positions and object mutation during __index__. Later faults refresh
  start/end/reason while preserving exception identity, original args and other
  handler mutations. Invalid encoder replacement rethrows that cached exception.
- `runtime-codec-registry.ts`: handleError also accepts a previously resolved
  runtime handler so kernels can retain per-operation callback identity without
  duplicating validation. Existing name-based callers remain supported.

Reference and TDD evidence:

- External oracle: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython 3.14.7, build
  `(main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`,
  Unicode 16.0.0, little-endian. Python is an external oracle only; unit tests
  never start Python or write files.
- Initial kernel, incremental and recovery suites failed to import the missing
  implementations. Four subsequent callback tests failed on absent recovery,
  output growth and cancellation handling, then passed after implementation.
  A metered incremental regression exposed negative allocation accounting when
  replacement input was longer than the original; accounting now follows the
  original-buffer slice, which is empty when consumption exceeds its length.
- Oracle probes confirm individual encoder surrogate error spans, three-byte
  UTF-16 high-surrogate truncation, and surrogatepass consuming a complete
  surrogate before reporting a remaining truncated byte. Existing UTF-8 kernels
  were left intact.
- An external guest comparison corrected an initially wrong identity assertion:
  CPython decode errors copy input bytes, while encode errors retain the source
  string. The exact nonidentity assertion failed before fixing the bridge.
  Another failing regression verified that invalid encoder replacements rethrow
  the cached mutated error, rather than publishing a new exception.
- Snapshot `src/runtime/__snapshots__/utf-wide-3.14.7.json`: **5,076 decode and
  336 encode cases**, SHA-256
  `41dcf30cf59c0f8faac63c38a5b6dcb2dc20b5a30d99591b8fb6afda5e53a187`.
  Includes BOMs, nulls, BMP/astral points, isolated/paired surrogates, invalid
  UTF-32 scalars, all prefixes of selected units and 25 random byte strings per
  width from Python Random(3147). Decoder inputs run all three byte-order modes,
  six policies and both final flags; encoders run six encodings/eight policies.
  Results retain code-point arrays, bytes, consumed counts, byte order and exact
  Unicode error fields. **5,412 matches**, executed inside two Vitest tests.
- Fresh-build external comparison: **1,404 decoder sequences and 336 encoder
  sequences, zero mismatches**. Decoder sequences compare both split calls and
  state after each return/error. Encoder sequences use seven setstate integers
  and successive surrogate, empty and astral inputs. These exercise real built
  kernels, not public modules or streams.
- Four source bodies from `runtime-wide-codec-guest.test.ts` were extracted with
  the TypeScript AST and run unchanged by CPython, binding fixture entry points
  to real codecs operations: **4 passed**. They cover handler/exception identity,
  input replacement, negative/index positions, validation, byte alignment and
  mutated exception rethrow. Fatal cancellation is tested in the interpreter;
  its separate body is not claimed as oracle evidence.

### 2026-09-11 — Reentrant incremental codec user-edge audit

Status: **unfinished**. This audit fixes UTF-16/32 internal state transitions;
`codec-registry`, `codec-utf16-32`, public integration and all unverified encoding
family rows remain open. Existing bounded family tasks and their scope remain
unchanged. No compatibility exceptions were introduced.

Reproduction and fixes:

- External oracle: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython **3.14.7** (main,
  Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49), Unicode **16.0.0**, little-endian. Oracle commands used
  real `codecs.getincrementaldecoder` / `getincrementalencoder` instances and
  `codecs.register_error`; Python was never invoked by the implementation.
- A decoder error callback calling `setstate((b'Q', 1))` must retain its new
  byte-order selection after an ordinary decode. For both widths, initial states
  0, 1 and 2 decode malformed input to `'?'` and leave `(b'', 1)`; the next
  big-endian `A` decodes as `A`. The implementation overwrote the selected state
  with 0 (or undecided 2). The new regression failed for each width before fixing.
- A callback cannot suppress a missing-BOM error by changing decoder state.
  With a complete malformed code unit but no BOM, both widths must raise
  `UnicodeDecodeError('utf-16'/'utf-32', input, 0, 2/4,
  'Stream does not start with BOM')`, retaining callback state `(b'Q', 1)`.
  The old implementation returned successfully instead; both regressions failed.
  A detected little-endian BOM, conversely, selects state 0 after successful
  recovery. Detection now branches on the state at call entry.
- After an encoder has emitted its first BOM, a callback's `reset()` must leave
  state 2 and cause the next call to emit a BOM. Both widths instead left state
  0; both regressions failed. Initial encoder selection now commits only when
  the call entered with no selected encoder. Reset during the first successful
  call still leaves state 0, matching CPython.
- Added eight parameterized internal tests covering state mutation, BOM failure
  and success, subsequent calls, guest failures and cancellation. Added two
  tests executing Python error handlers through real interpreter calls,
  UnicodeError storage and `RuntimeCodecRecovery`. These guest tests bind
  internal incremental operations explicitly; they do not claim that public
  codec imports or codec classes are implemented.
- Independent CPython assertions passed for the two guest sequences and for
  callback-failure state retention. Cancellation is checked against the sandbox
  execution contract: cancellation dominates callback failure, while callback
  mutations already performed remain observable in the internal state.

all encoding-family tasks and the existing 1,411 module/API inventory rows open.
This change implements the missing bytes-instance decode invocation path; it
is not completion of codec modules, the bytes type or shared registry assembly.

Validated before implementation:

- `session-decode-compatibility.test.ts`: **22/22 failed** because the public
  session returned `exception` for calls to the absent bytes `decode` member.
  The previous public probe above records the exact AttributeError.
- The identical 22 guest source strings in `decode-compatibility-cases.ts`
  passed on `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`: **CPython 3.14.7**, build
  `main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49`, Clang 21.0.0; `unicodedata.unidata_version`
  **16.0.0**. Python was used only as an external differential oracle.
- Oracle command: emit `JSON.stringify(decodeCases)` with `npx tsx`, pipe
  to that Python executable, load the JSON and execute each source in its own
  dictionary. Output: `22 CPython cases passed`. No Python is invoked by the
  runtime or unit tests.

Implementation and exact evidence:

| API / behavior | Evidence | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b'hello'.decode()` and UTF-8 non-ASCII input | `session-decode-compatibility`, cases 0–1 | invocation verified |
| Latin-1 and UTF-8 signature decoding | same file, cases 2–3 | invocation verified |
| Empty receiver skips unknown codec/error lookup; valid input skips unused error-handler lookup | cases 4–5 | invocation verified |
| ASCII `ignore`, `replace`, `backslashreplace`, `surrogateescape` | cases 6–9, exact output including lone surrogate | invocation verified |
| Argument type errors, keyword suggestions, duplicate position/name, positional and keyword arity | cases 10–15, exact exception args | invocation verified |
| Embedded NUL in either name, including empty receiver | cases 16–17 | invocation verified |
| Surrogate encoding-name failure | case 18: original name identity and exact encoding/start/end/reason | invocation verified |
| Encoding/error str subtypes bypass `__str__` and `__len__` | case 19 | invocation verified |
| ASCII UnicodeDecodeError attributes | case 20: encoding/object/start/end/reason, args, cause/context | invocation verified; full tracebacks remain open |
| Nonempty unknown encoding | case 21: exact LookupError args | invocation verified |
| Supplied registry uses its successful lookup cache and ignores consumed-count value | `runtime-bytes-decode-method.test.ts`: `uses the supplied registry, cached codec identity and unchecked consumed counts` | internal integration evidence only |
| Wrong decoder result type | same file: `validates registry decoder output after tuple extraction` | internal integration evidence only |
| Empty receiver and name validation order | same file: `validates names but skips the codec for an empty receiver` | internal integration evidence only |
| Cancellation after return or throw | same file: two `cancellation dominates decoder return and failure` cases | internal integration evidence only |

`runtime-codec-arguments.ts` extracts the existing `str.encode` argument
binding for both consumers. `runtime-bytes-decode-method.ts` invokes the same
text-decoder policy and result validation used by str construction. The public
native-attribute path installs the existing native text decoder. **It does not
assemble or publish the interpreter-owned registry**: that remains required.
The registry-backed method tests supply a real RuntimeCodecRegistry explicitly;
those tests are not public module registration evidence.

Fresh public probes after implementation, each through current-source
`PythonSession` with 200,000 steps, 4,000,000 allocated bytes, depth 100 and
hash seed `[1n, 2n]`:

| --- | --- | --- |
| `codecs` | import terminated / capability / `runtime operation has no installed capability` | every existing API row open |
| `_codecs` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings.aliases` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings.ascii` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings.latin_1` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings.utf_8` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `encodings.charmap` | same import termination | every existing API row open |
| `type(b'A')` | terminated / capability / `canonical type for bytes is unavailable` | open |
| `bytes('A', 'utf-8')` | `NameError("name 'bytes' is not defined")` | open |
| `open('codec.txt', encoding='utf-8')` | `NameError("name 'open' is not defined")` | open |
| `b'A'.decode.__self__` | `AttributeError("'builtin_function_or_method' object has no attribute '__self__'")` | method metadata/descriptors open |

Required remaining work is unchanged: real import/module behavior, CodecInfo
metadata and tuple subclass behavior, public search/error registration, owned
module inventories including charmap, incremental classes and stream adapters,
shared registry wiring for all consumers and source decoding, exact fast paths,
all remaining subtype/descriptors/introspection behavior, exception tracebacks,
callback suspension/resumption and cancellation through actual supported service
adapters. The unavailable APIs above are blockers, not accepted differences.
No module/API rows or reference cases were removed or declared out of scope.

### 2026-09-11 pinned Unicode encodings: escape kernels and complete module surface inventory

Status: **unfinished**. Keep `codec-registry`, `codec-registry-integration`,
`codec-unicode-transforms`, all ten Unicode module tasks and every other
unverified codec-family task open. Component and consumer evidence below does
not verify unavailable public classes, imports, streams or descriptors.
No compatibility exception, skipped required case or narrowed target is accepted.

Reference: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython **3.14.7**,
`main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49`, Clang 21.0.0, native **little** endian,
`unicodedata.unidata_version == '16.0.0'`. Used only outside the implementation
and unit tests as a differential oracle. Source inspected:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/unicodeobject.c
(Unicode Escape and Raw Unicode Escape sections). No runtime Python, host eval,
ambient Unicode tables, ambient I/O or LLM calls were introduced.

Reproduced before implementing:

- `runtime/unicode-escape.test.ts`: failed suite with `Cannot find module
  './unicode-escape.js'`. The two escape kernels were absent.
- Added incremental split cases: failed with `UnicodeEscapeDecoder is not a
  constructor`, then implemented owned buffering.
- Differential escape row `\\N{TANGUT IDEOGRAPH-17000}`: package raised
  `UnicodeDecodeError('unicodeescape', input, 0, 26,
  'unknown Unicode character name')`; pinned oracle returned U+17000, consumed 26.
  Four Tangut boundary lookup assertions and the generator range assertion
  subsequently failed before the table-generator correction.
- `session-escape-encoding.test.ts`: all **6 cases failed**, returning
  `exception` because escape encoders were not in native text dispatch.
  All six exact guest source strings also passed on the pinned external oracle.

Implementation:

- `runtime/unicode-escape.ts`: package-owned Unicode/raw escape encode/decode;
  raw backslash pair handling, Latin-1 input interpretation, short/octal/hex/name
  escapes, exact malformed/truncated/out-of-range spans and reasons, consumed
  counts, incomplete-input handling, surrogate preservation, strict/ignore/
  replace/backslashreplace/surrogateescape/surrogatepass behavior and explicit
  error-recovery service. Callback input replacement/resume and allocation growth
  are metered; cancellation dominates callback return and throw.
- Warning service is required by the decode kernel, not silently discarded.
  Only the first invalid escape produces the CPython DeprecationWarning message,
  after decoding succeeds. Warning exceptions prevent incremental buffer commit.
  Public warning filters, category objects, locations and tracebacks are still
  required through real guest warning integration.
- Owned incremental decoder copies restored/exported buffers, ignores the second
  state item, resets, and commits only after successful decoding and warning
  emission. Octal escapes can depend on chunk boundaries in CPython; the oracle
  corpus compares those actual outputs instead of imposing false equivalence
  with one-shot decoding.
- Native text encoder dispatch now recognizes `unicode_escape` and
  `raw_unicode_escape`. These encoders accept every code point and therefore
  never resolve the error handler, including an unused unknown handler.
- Generated Unicode 16 name ranges now include Tangut. `generate:unicode` fetched
  the existing SHA-256-pinned UCD inputs and regenerated the tables. The existing
  reverse-name behavior remains intact: CPython lookup accepts Tangut names but
  `unicodedata.name(chr(0x17000), None)` returns None. The reverse lookup explicitly
  preserves that asymmetry. Unrelated existing edits were retained.

Exact evidence keys for the inventory below:

| Key | Evidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 | Fresh current-source `PythonSession` import of each of the ten modules, limits maxSteps=200000/maxAllocatedBytes=4000000/maxDepth=100, hashSeed=[1n,2n] | Every import returned exactly `{"status":"terminated","reason":"capability","message":"runtime operation has no installed capability"}`; every module/API row below remains open |
| U2 | `runtime/__snapshots__/unicode-escape-3.14.7.json`, replayed by `runtime/unicode-escape.test.ts` | 10,680 decode rows with exact points/consumed counts or encoding/object/start/end/reason, plus exact warning category/message; 6 encode rows |
| U3 | Same snapshot, `incremental` | 1,128 two-call scenarios, every byte split of ten selected inputs for both codecs and all six decode policies; exact per-call outputs/errors/warnings and buffered state |
| U4 | `session-escape-encoding.test.ts` | 6 real interpreter cases, also executed verbatim by the pinned oracle: empty input, controls, Latin-1, astral text, separate surrogates, all eight standard policies plus unused unknown policy, and Tangut source name lookup |
| U5 | Export every explicit generated name plus every point in every algorithmic range; run actual `lookupUnicodeName` for uppercase and lowercase; compare each with oracle `codecs.unicode_escape_decode` | **310,950 comparisons, zero mismatches**; not a claim about arbitrary invalid names or public unicodedata module APIs |
| U6 | Encode a CodePointString containing each integer in `[0, 0x110000)` in order; independently encode the same oracle string, compare SHA-256 bytes | `unicode_escape`: `050b614f71f0864d3f518694db09463bc23b0f88c23fa4853e03d82aa5e139f2`; `raw_unicode_escape`: `88ac5734deced15b9acc6dd9bfd9fba16c3764fee1e90909eb960046132ff77c`; both match, including all 2,048 surrogates |
| U7 | `runtime/unicode-escape.test.ts` recovery, warning and metering cases | Replaced callback input, 100-point replacement growth, warning-error buffer preservation, reset/state copying, cancellation on callback return/throw and bounded nonadvancing recovery |

Validated failures before fixes:

1. `runtime/unicode-recovery-state.test.ts`: both tests failed. For UTF-7 input
   `[255,65,255]`, a callback replacing `error.object` with empty bytes and returning
   `('?',0)` produced consumed=0 instead of the reference consumed=3 on final
   decoding. Incremental final decoding retained `[255,65,255]` instead of empty
   buffered state. The same missing final-consumption rule affected UTF-8,
   UTF-8 signature, UTF-16 and UTF-32 state. Escape codecs also had the wrong
   consumed count when a replacement input was exhausted on a nonfinal call.
2. `session-unicode-text-consumers.test.ts`: all 70 groups failed before wiring.
   Native dispatch had no UTF-7 or UTF-16/32 entries, despite existing kernels.
   The reference source bodies exercise encoding, bytes decoding and str(bytes).
3. After wiring, seven consumer groups still failed on surrogate policies. For
   example, `b'\xff\xfe\x00'.decode('utf_32','surrogateescape')` must have
   `error.args == ('utf-32-le', b'\xff\xfe\x00', 0, 3, 'truncated data')`
   but live start=2/end=3. The implementation reconstructed args from the last
   fault. `session-unicode-error-cache.test.ts` added three more failing public
   cases for UTF-8, UTF-8 signature and UTF-7 before the metadata fix.
4. `session-escape-decoding.test.ts`: all 18 groups failed before decoding was
   wired. Both escape encoders were already correct and were retained.

`runtime-unicode-text-codecs.ts` now declares the shared native codec bindings and
pinned aliases. Existing str.encode, bytes.decode and str(bytes) dispatch use
those kernels; UTF-7, all six wide codecs and both escape decoders no longer
raise an unknown-encoding error for supported names. Escape warnings route
through `BuiltinInvocationContext.warn` and the execution's explicit service.
Missing warning service is not silently ignored. Full warning filters, category
objects and guest promotion of warnings remain unfinished requirements.

Final UTF-7/8/16/32 decoding returns the original input length, even when a
callback replaces the input. Nonfinal decoding returns the replacement-input
cursor. Escape decoding returns the original input length whenever the current
input is exhausted, including nonfinal calls; incomplete escapes return their
cursor. Buffering continues to slice the original combined input, as CPython
requires. No error-callback state mutation or original-buffer ownership was
removed. Internal decode faults can retain initial error-location metadata;
guest exception preparation now creates initial args separately from live fields.

Four older recovery assertions had encoded incorrect consumption expectations.
Their exact inputs/callback positions were independently rerun on the pinned
oracle before correcting those expectations: UTF-7 `+ABC-` => consumed **5**;
UTF-16-LE `[00,dc]` => **2**; Unicode escape `A\uQ` => **4**; BOM-prefixed UTF-8
`[ef,bb,bf,ff]` => **4**. Output and callback assertions were retained. These are
reference corrections, not weakened assertions or removed cases.

Implemented:

- `single-byte-encode.ts` accepts the existing registry-validated recovery
  contract. It groups adjacent unencodable source points, passes original
  source spans, accepts arbitrary replacement bytes, validates replacement
  text against the selected 128/256 range, and resumes at the validated index.
  Rejection uses `RuntimeCodecRecovery`'s cached-exception restoration hook;
  replacement text is not recursively recovered. Existing built-in policies
  and surrogate handling remain covered.
- `single-byte-decode.ts` supplies the shared ASCII/Latin-1 decoder, including
  all six existing built-in decode policies, explicit registry recovery,
  callback replacement of the input object, original input consumption,
  metered backwards resumes, failures and cancellation. Ordinary
  `runtime-text-decoding.ts` now uses it while retaining lazy unknown-handler
  lookup, aliases, empty-input behavior, and explicit fallback dispatch.
- Compiled guest bindings in `runtime-wide-codec-guest.test.ts` exercise the
  real registry, recovery adapter, exception storage and invocation machinery
  for both encoders and the ASCII decoder. They verify negative positions,
  `__index__` replacement of error.object, original args, handler caching during
  an operation, registration effects on the next call, cached error identity,
  restoration of rejected replacement spans/reason, retained object/encoding
  mutations, guest failure identity and cancellation. These internal bindings
  are explicitly **not** public-import or stream compatibility evidence.

Status: **unfinished**. No codec inventory row is closed. `codec-registry`,

row remain open. Added bounded `codec-charmap-build` and

Validated gap and implementation:

- Existing `SingleByteTableCodec` owns fixed integer tables and cannot execute
  arbitrary guest mappings, their `__getitem__` effects, or one-to-many results.
  The new test first failed resolving absent `runtime-charmap.js`. Compiled
  guest tests then failed with NameError for the absent internal fixture bindings.
- `runtime/runtime-charmap.ts` implements arbitrary encode/decode mapping
  execution via the real `runtimeGetItem` protocol. It validates native integer,
  bool, bytes and str payloads without invoking conversion overrides; handles
  missing/None entries, LookupError subclasses, empty/multicharacter results,
  U+FFFE sentinels, integer bounds and Python type diagnostics. Encoding preserves
  CPython's lookahead and repeated lookup side effects when delimiting undefined
  spans, and maps replacement text through the original mapping. Raw replacement
  bytes bypass mapping. None mapping uses the existing Latin-1 kernel.
- Existing registry recovery supplies validated guest callbacks. Decode recovery
  can replace input and use a negative __index__ resume relative to that replacement;
  consumed counts retain original input length. Failed replacement encoding retains
  the cached guest exception identity and restores its original span/reason.
  Mapping failures propagate through ordinary interpreter exceptions. Cancellation
  remains an uncatchable execution termination. No existing fixed-table, UTF,
  newline or conversion implementation was replaced.

Implemented after reproducing the instruction gap:

- `src/runtime/runtime-import-statement.ts` executes `import` and `from`
  instructions through the active frame's guest builtin `__import__` hook.
  It passes the original globals/locals, `None` for optimized-frame locals,
  the exact fromlist and relative level; resolves aliases through attributes;
  and keeps earlier bindings when a later import fails. Each ordinary import
  in a comma-separated statement looks up the hook again.
- Star imports index `__all__`, rather than iterating it. Without `__all__`,
  they snapshot dictionary keys and omit underscore-prefixed names. Partial
  bindings and callback exceptions survive. Missing attributes on nonmodule
  return objects produce ImportError with `name`, `name_from`, and null path,
  without retaining the swallowed AttributeError as exception context.
- `runtime-program.ts` uses that instruction path in ordinary and suspended
  frames. `error.ts` admits native ImportError. The existing frame-cleanup
  regression now asserts the exact missing-hook ImportError and retains its
  earlier binding/depth assertions.
- No module objects, module loader, fake codec module, host capability, host
  Python invocation, eval or source rewriting was added to the runtime.
  `runtime-codec-registry.ts` was read but not changed in this prerequisite.

A5 reproducer (external oracle `compile(source, 'bad_source.py', 'exec')`
and real public `PythonSession.exec(source, {filename: 'bad_source.py'})`):

```python
source = b"# coding: utf-8\nvalue = '\xff'\n"
```

CPython raises SyntaxError with exact args:

```python
("Non-UTF-8 code starting with '\\xff' on line 2, but no encoding declared; see https://peps.python.org/pep-0263/ for details",
 (None, 2, 10, "value = '�'", 2, 10))
```

The interpreter instead returns a diagnostic with message
`'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 25: invalid start byte`,
filename `bad_source.py`, position `{offset: 0, line: 0, column: -2}`, and no
source line/end position. Changing the cookie to `utf8` or `utf8.ucs2` makes
CPython use registry decoding and produce the ordinary codec-error diagnostic
with whole-input byte offsets; those probes match the interpreter. The
canonical/default UTF-8 tokenizer path therefore must remain distinct from
registry alias decoding. Required follow-up includes tokenizer error ordering,
physical-line attribution, replacement-decoded error text, null filename,
end offsets, and guest compile/exec exception attributes and tracebacks.
Neither the alias fix nor the passing A2 corpus resolves A5.

## Core codec binding work and retained failing integration gates — 2026-09-11

Status: **unfinished**. The complete CPython 3.14.7 / Darwin / Unicode 16.0.0
requirement remains unchanged. `codec-core-guest-api`, `codec-registry-integration`

Implemented a package-owned binding component,
`packages/safe-python/src/runtime/runtime-core-codec-functions.ts`, for
`ascii_encode`, `latin_1_encode`, `utf_8_encode`, `ascii_decode`,
`latin_1_decode` and `utf_8_decode`. These functions take an explicitly owned
`RuntimeCodecRegistry` and invoke `RuntimeCodecRecovery` with the real
interpreter invocation context. They are **not yet published by modules or
installed in PythonSession**. They do not establish public guest API coverage.
No substitute modules or new test-only runtime entry points were installed.

Binding behavior implemented and exercised:

- Positional-only argument count/keyword validation; native string payloads;
  `errors=None`; strict UTF-8 conversion of error names; NUL rejection; lazy
  handler lookup including empty inputs; UTF-8 `final=False` by default.
- ASCII/Latin-1/UTF-8 result tuples and consumed counts, including UTF-8's
  nonfinal cursor after a decoder callback replaces its input.
- Single-byte and UTF-8 recovery through one registry adapter, including
  retained source-subtype identity, cached exception identity and original
  args, negative `__index__`, tuple/string subtype storage, mutated decode
  objects, rejected replacement fields and cancellation.
- CPython's distinct native error fast paths. ASCII/Latin-1 strict encoding
  bypasses registered strict callbacks; UTF-8 strict encoding resolves the
  callback. Surrogateescape consumes its native prefix before recovering the
  next invalid span. The kernels gained an optional recovery argument for
  that remaining span; existing callers retain their existing behavior.
- Decoder buffer leases are acquired before later argument conversion, copied
  after final truth conversion, and released on success, invalid errors,
  final-conversion failures and cancellation. These lease tests use explicit
  mocked services in fast unit tests; real public buffer adapter validation
  remains required. No iterable or `__bytes__` coercion was added.

and duplicate checks, missing-required/unknown-keyword ordering and spelling
suggestions. Name conversion reads native string subtype payloads without calling
__str__, rejects NUL, and preserves the original object when a surrogate name
raises UnicodeEncodeError. General encode/decode preserve the distinction between
omitted errors (one codec argument) and explicitly supplied strict (two codec
arguments). Registry mutation, successful cache identity, error-handler lookup,
replacement and removal retain their existing implementation. Cancellation is
checked on return and failure.

`runtime-codec-registry.ts` itself was inspected and left unchanged; the fix is

Implemented one reproduced observable mismatch in
`src/runtime/runtime-string-decoding.ts`: after validating decoder output,
canonicalize empty strings and single Latin-1 characters to the session's exact
str singletons. Preserve every other returned string object's identity,
including str subclasses. Read native code-point storage without invoking
`__str__`, `__len__`, `__getitem__` or buffer conversion on the result. General
registry decode keeps the original codec result, and encoding continues to
preserve bytes subtypes. The existing buffer-lease cleanup and cancellation
paths remain in place.

The distinction is essential: CPython does **not** strip every decoder-returned
str subtype. The exact implementation is `unicode_result` and its invocation
at the end of `PyUnicode_Decode` in
[CPython v3.14.7 Objects/unicodeobject.c](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.7/Objects/unicodeobject.c#L748).
The former replaces empty/one-byte singleton values and otherwise returns the
original object. This corrects the earlier unconditional subtype-identity
expectation in `runtime-text-codec-result.test.ts`; it does not relax result
validation or any failing traceback/import assertion.

### 2026-09-11 — UTF-16/32 rejected replacement cache restoration

Status: **unfinished**. No codec family or public API inventory row is closed.
`codec-registry` remains open. A parsed YAML audit found
`codec-registry-integration.status.test: done` despite failing public imports;
changed that scalar to `open` using its parsed source range, preserving other

test statuses. Existing bounded family tasks remain in this same pipeline:
UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16/32, UTF-7, Unicode escapes, single-byte tables/charmap, Chinese,
Japanese, Korean, ISO-2022 Japanese/Korean, HZ, IDNA, binary transforms and
platform codecs, with separate guest API, stream and consumer integration rows.

**Validated mismatch and implementation**

CPython 3.14.7 restores a cached UnicodeEncodeError's start/end/reason when a
UTF-16/32 error callback supplies unencodable replacement text or raw bytes
whose length is not divisible by the code-unit width. It retains callback
mutations to object and encoding, original args, and exception identity. This
restoration happens after replacement-position __index__ side effects, including
negative resume positions, and applies when an earlier fault already populated
the cached exception.

Before this change, utf-wide.ts threw the cached failure without restoring its
location/reason. Added 24 compiled guest regressions spanning both widths,
BOM/native, little-endian and big-endian modes, text/raw replacements, and first
versus reused faults. All failed at `rejected replacement location` before the
runtime change. WideEncodeRecovery now accepts the existing registry recovery
rejection callback; both rejection paths call it before propagating the cached
failure. RuntimeCodecRecovery performs the field restoration. Existing fallback
kernel failures, successful replacements, handler validation and budget behavior
are retained. No host codec, Python runtime delegation, eval, filesystem or LLM
capability was added.

Files touched in this increment: src/runtime/utf-wide.ts,
src/runtime/runtime-codec-recovery.ts,
src/runtime/runtime-wide-codec-guest.test.ts,
src/codec-public-contract-cases.ts and this plan. Pre-existing edits were
preserved. No README, root CLI, commit, push or release changes.

Status: **unfinished**. No public codec module or encoding-family inventory row
is closed by this change. The parsed YAML pipeline had
`codec-registry.status.test: done` despite failing public integration gates;

Implemented `src/runtime/punycode.ts`: package-owned, stateless Punycode encoding
and decoding using exact integer arithmetic and guest code points. Covers ASCII
segregation, repeated/nonbasic code points, bias adaptation, case-insensitive
encoded digits, malformed digits, incomplete input, ASCII-prefix failures,
strict/replace/ignore behavior, out-of-range decoded characters and Py_ssize_t
conversion overflow. Lone surrogates remain code points. No host Unicode, IDNA,
codec, filesystem, process or network capability is used by the implementation.
Integer growth and insertion work are metered; cancellation remains fatal.

Added Punycode to the existing declarative Unicode text codec table, exposing it
through actual `PythonSession` str.encode, bytes.decode and str(bytes) execution.
The native decoder now forwards the requested policy name to its codec instead
of replacing unknown names with strict before the call. This is necessary for
Punycode's eager rejection of unsupported policies, including valid nonempty
input. Existing Unicode kernels still raise at a fault and retain the existing
fallback/error-handler path. Empty native byte conversion behavior is unchanged.
This is **not** evidence that these consumers share the missing public registry.

Punycode's incomplete and overflow faults reproduced a separate native
`PythonDecodeError` defect: formatting an out-of-object single-byte span indexed
undefined host storage and raised a host TypeError. Its constructor now formats
those spans as CPython's byte ranges. Positions are generic over number/bigint,
so Punycode faults above JavaScript's exact-number range retain exact guest
exception fields and args. Other kernels retain numeric locations. Added
UnicodeError to the internal native exception-name union for Punycode's explicit
policy validation.

### 2026-09-11 — Punycode rewritten-error chains and Py_ssize_t overflow audit

Status: **unfinished**. No public codec module, API inventory or encoding-family
row is closed. Parsed the pipeline YAML and found
`codec-registry.status.implement: done` despite the reproduced public gates;
changed only that scalar to `open` using its parsed source range. All 32 existing
bounded `codec-` rows now retain open implementation and test statuses, including
Chinese/Japanese/Korean, ISO-2022 Japanese/Korean, HZ, IDNA, binary transforms,
platform codecs, Punycode public APIs and the stream/consumer integration rows.
No duplicate family tasks or alternative plan were added.

Concrete mismatches reproduced and corrected:

- Punycode rewrites ASCII-prefix and extended-suffix UnicodeDecodeError instances
  with the complete original byte input and adjusted positions. CPython retains
  the original exception in `__context__`, sets `__cause__` to None and
  `__suppress_context__` to True. The implementation previously discarded that
  original error and did not suppress its context.
- The inner suffix exception uses uppercase suffix bytes and relative positions;
  the ASCII error uses only the bytes preceding the last delimiter. Both retain
  the caller's active handled exception. Truncated generalized integers retain an
  additional `IndexError('index out of range')` between the inner decode error and
  the caller's exception.
- `b'A-hz767205604493046e'` produces an inner error with positions
  `(9223372036854775806, 9223372036854775807)`. Adding the prefix offset overflows
  while constructing the rewritten error, so the final OverflowError retains
  that inner UnicodeDecodeError without suppression. Adjacent vectors beginning
  `A-iz` and `A-jz` overflow while constructing the inner error instead and retain
  only the caller's active exception. This distinct second bug was reproduced
  after the initial chaining correction, before its own fix.

`PythonRuntimeError` now carries explicit package-owned exception-chain metadata;
`PythonDecodeError` accepts that metadata and `RuntimeExceptionExecution.prepare`
materializes it using real guest exception storage. Punycode supplies the inner
errors, suffix/prefix objects and suppression only where its pinned Python codec
would do so. Extra byte copies and exception preparation remain metered. Existing
unrelated edits, native fast paths and error fields were preserved. No host codec,
Python runtime delegation, eval, external service, filesystem or LLM call was
added to interpreter execution or unit tests.

Files changed in this correction: `src/runtime/error.ts`,
`src/runtime/decode-error.ts`, `src/runtime/runtime-exception-execution.ts`,
`src/runtime/punycode.ts`, `src/session-punycode-error-chain.test.ts`,
`src/codec-public-contract-cases.ts` and this plan.

### Byte escape API audit and implementation (2026-09-12)

Status: **unfinished**. No codec API or inventory row is closed. A parsed YAML
audit again found `codec-registry.status.implement: done`; changed that scalar
to `open` through its parsed source range after reproducing the public failures.
All 38 codec rows now have open implementation and test statuses. The existing
`codec-buffer-escape-api` row owns this work; its public integration requirements
and every other family requirement remain unchanged.

Implemented `runtime/runtime-byte-escape.ts` and installed `escape_encode` and
`escape_decode` in the existing core function factory. Encoding requires native
bytes storage and returns fresh nonempty bytes, including one-byte results;
empty results remain canonical. Decoding accepts native bytes, strict UTF-8 text
or an explicitly supplied contiguous buffer lease. It implements byte escapes,
octal wrapping, malformed hex recovery and trailing-backslash errors. Neither
operation uses host codecs or Unicode tables. Error-name validation, text
conversion precedence and retained Unicode error source objects use existing
runtime machinery. Decoding deliberately supports only the reference's native
hex-error policies; registering an arbitrary codec handler does not change that
contract. This is CPython behavior, not a compatibility exception.

Invalid escape warnings use the explicit interpreter warning service, preserve
the first invalid escape and run only after successful decoding. Warning
failures propagate; cancellation remains fatal even when a service also throws.
Buffer exports are released after success, validation/copy/warning failure and
cancellation. Encoder buffer coercion is rejected without invoking exporters.
The existing small-byte factory supports fresh allocation; no object-layer
shortcut or host capability was introduced.

The external reference is `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`: CPython 3.14.7,
`main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49`, Clang 21.0.0, Unicode 16.0.0. Reviewed the pinned
[CPython byte escape implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.7/Objects/bytesobject.c)
and queried the actual oracle for results, warning order, argument diagnostics
and result identities. Python runs only as an external oracle, never inside the
implementation or unit tests.

## Builtin publication and native allocator audit — 2026-09-12

Status: **unfinished**. The `native-types` implementation and test statuses remain
open. The target remains CPython 3.14.7 on the pinned platform with Unicode
16.0.0; this audit does not establish complete builtin compatibility. In
particular, publication and descriptor-category matches never count as complete
method implementations. Missing publication, unavailable services, and entries
without behavioral coverage remain blockers.

### Reference and inventory evidence

The external differential oracle was `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`:
CPython 3.14.7 (main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49), Clang 21.0.0,
`sys.platform == 'darwin'`, `platform.machine() == 'arm64'`,
`sys.maxsize == 9223372036854775807`, Unicode 16.0.0, normal site-enabled startup.
Host Python was used only to capture reference data, never to implement guest
execution. Runtime and test execution use the real TypeScript interpreter.

New artifacts under `packages/safe-python/src/runtime/__snapshots__/`:

| Artifact | Evidence and limits |
| --- | --- |
| `builtin-member-inventory-3.14.7.json` | All 159 names in the pinned `vars(builtins)`, categorized as exception, type, function/callable or constant. Includes builtin module metadata and site-installed helpers. Also 185 type access paths and 6,415 member rows: every declaration reachable through the MRO of each enumerated type, with defining owner, MRO index, descriptor category, and whether the declaration is local. |
| `builtin-member-observations.json` | Actual public `PythonSession` publication results for every captured name and declaration. Records exact guest error names/messages and capability/internal termination results. A blocked owner retains its failure and blocks its member probes; these are not passes or skipped compatibility cases. All rows retain `behavior: unverified` because these probes do not prove the complete behavior contract. |
| `builtin-binding-3.14.7.json` | 210 oracle calls spanning 30 builtin functions: zero through four positional arguments, an unexpected keyword alone, and a positional argument plus unexpected keyword. Exact result types/representations or error types/messages are retained. |
| `builtin-exception-publication-3.14.7.json` | 52 oracle cases covering the two newly published exception types, native allocation, subtype payloads, explicit descriptors, keyword validation, reinitialization, multiple inheritance, and allocator overrides. |

The type census includes every type directly published by `builtins`, type
exports from `types`, and explicit access paths for bytearray/memoryview,
collection views, forward/reverse/callable iterators, long-range iterators,
generic aliases and their iterators, unions, descriptors, bound methods,
generators/coroutines and their suspension objects, cells, code/frame/traceback
objects, optimized frame locals, and code-position/line iterators. Alternate
paths intentionally retain aliases. This is an enumerated census, not a proof
that every internally reachable CPython type has been discovered. Metaclass
member implementations are inventoried through `type`; dynamically synthesized
attributes and all invocation semantics still require their own behavioral
cases. String methods were left unchanged.

The final public census reports:

- 120 builtin names permit a type-name read; 39 are absent from the actual
  builtin namespace. Looking up module globals instead would incorrectly hide
  missing builtin module metadata, so probes read `__builtins__[name]` directly.
- `enumerate`, `filter`, `map`, `reversed`, and `zip` are published as
  `builtin_function_or_method`, while the reference publishes types.
- Of 185 type-path setups, 100 evaluate, 62 raise guest exceptions, and 23
  terminate because required runtime capabilities/canonical types are absent.
  Successful setup alone does not establish that the object is a canonical type.
- Of 6,415 member rows, 2,729 descriptor-category reads succeed, 829 raise guest
  exceptions, and 2,857 are blocked by their owner setup. Successful descriptor
  categories match the reference, but that says nothing about correct calling,
  binding, storage, introspection or mutation behavior.

### Reproduced fixes

`MemoryError` and `_IncompleteInputError` were absent from the exception catalog
and therefore absent from the public builtin namespace. The original 35 public
regression cases all failed before implementation. Added catalog entries rather
than an independent publication list or guest stubs; the registry and session
already derive exception publication from this catalog.

`MemoryError` has a distinct native allocator despite sharing base exception
storage. Exact `MemoryError.__new__(MemoryError, ...)` initializes empty args;
subclass allocation captures positional args. `__init__` retains the existing
exception initializer, including keyword rejection, while subclass overrides can
accept keywords. `_IncompleteInputError` inherits the real SyntaxError allocator,
initializer and fields and publishes its reference documentation.

The mixed `MemoryError`/`StopIteration` cases reproduced a difference between
native allocation during a type call and an explicit `__new__` descriptor call.
Native type calls now select the layout's allocation family when a native
`__new__` wrapper supplies the slot. Explicit descriptor calls retain subtype
and allocator-safety validation. Function overrides keep their normal dispatch;
unsafe-allocation diagnostics walk the layout bases to name the static allocator
selected after an override. The corpus covers both base orders, native wrapper
assignments (including an unrelated `int.__new__`), guest function overrides,
exact/subclass args, descriptor ownership, and retained SyntaxError fields after
reinitialization. These fixes do not introduce ambient capabilities.

Sources used to verify the allocation distinction:
[CPython 3.14.7 exception implementations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/exceptions.c),
[CPython 3.14.7 type allocation and tp_new wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/typeobject.c).

The broad regression run exposed an old test expecting a native `MemoryError`
to escape guest exception normalization as unsupported. Its original input now
has a positive test checking canonical guest identity, preserved arguments,
handler execution and restored exception state. Separate unsupported `OSError`
and name-spoofed host-error checks remain. No assertion failure was excluded or
turned into an expected failure.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Initial exception reproduction | 35/35 cases failed while the names were absent. |
| Expanded oracle reproduction | Three failures after initial publication exposed exact-versus-subclass args and both mixed-base allocation paths; two further failures exposed native wrapper assignment and static-base diagnostic selection. Fixed without changing oracle outcomes. |
| Broad focused workspace tests | `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- session-builtin-binding.test.ts session-exception-publication.test.ts runtime-type builtin-type class-definition class-bases metaclass type-instantiation runtime-exception exception-state builtin-exception runtime-native runtime-integer-construction runtime-float-construction runtime-complex-construction runtime-string-construction runtime-set-construction`: **1,827 passed**, 38 files, 13.40 seconds, no skips. This run contained the then-current 46 exception cases. |
| Final expanded public corpus | `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- session-exception-publication.test.ts session-builtin-binding.test.ts`: **262 passed**, 2 files, 5.83 seconds; 52 exception cases plus all 210 binding cases, no skips. |
| Workspace typecheck | `npm run typecheck --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`: passed after implementation and integration-test changes. |
| Scoped ESLint | Passed for both new session test files and `builtin-exception-new.ts`, `standard-exception-catalog.ts`, `runtime-type-registry.ts`, `runtime-type-layout.ts`, `runtime-type-call.ts`, `runtime-type-new-integration.test.ts`. |

The binding corpus initially matched all fixed values/errors. The raw oracle
numbers for `id(None)` and `hash(None)` differ across interpreter processes, as
allowed by their contracts. Their rows retain the captured numbers and explicitly
record that limitation; tests require integer results and stability within the
session, with distinct identities for the retained singleton objects. They do
not normalize away error messages, values, mutation or other meaningful
observations. The other 208 rows compare exact outputs. These argument probes
are limited evidence, not complete implementation certificates for the 30 APIs.

All unit cases run in memory, without LLM calls, filesystem fixtures, mocked
interpreter components, or host-Python delegation. No build was needed for these
source-based tests/typecheck. No CLI visuals changed, so no CLI screenshot was
applicable. No README files, commits, pushes or releases were made.

### Remaining blockers and continuation procedure

The 39 absent builtin namespace entries are the OSError family and aliases,
BaseExceptionGroup/ExceptionGroup, builtin module metadata, `__import__`,
`breakpoint`, `bytearray`, `bytes`, `memoryview`, `property`, `dir`, `open`, and
site-installed helpers (`copyright`, `credits`, `exit`, `help`, `license`,
`quit`). Exact names and errors are in the observation artifact. Iterator type
publication and native iterator identities remain unimplemented. Many exposed
types still lack owned descriptors or metadata; the artifact records each
failed declaration read, including reflective function/code/frame/traceback and
suspension members. Generic alias construction/publication and `types` imports
also remain blocked. No placeholder or present-but-unverified member is counted
as complete.

Real I/O and import service adapters have not been implemented or verified by
this change. `print`/`input` already have dedicated factories with explicit
session services; the census does not establish their complete CPython behavior.
`open`, imports, module publication, service suspension, full buffers, exception
tracebacks/warnings, every remaining descriptor contract, and unverified builtin
members remain requirements of this same plan. Neither new exception type is a
certificate of full exception API compatibility, and resource-exhaustion
semantics remain part of the overall compatibility audit.

To continue this audit manually:

1. Verify the oracle version, Unicode data, architecture, maximum integer index,
   and site-enabled startup against the reference metadata before comparison.
2. Read all builtin entries from `vars(builtins)`. For each reference type path,
   execute its recorded setup, enumerate the union of its MRO dictionaries, and
   record the first declaring MRO index, owner and raw descriptor type. Preserve
   aliases and add newly discovered paths; do not remove blocked entries.
3. In a fresh real `PythonSession` for each owner, execute its recorded setup and
   evaluate the type expression. Read each declaration using
   `type(audit_type.__mro__[mroIndex].__dict__[member]).__name__`. Record owner
   exceptions/terminations and member exceptions exactly. The observation
   artifact is evidence of current failures, not a golden expected-result test.
4. For each suspected behavior mismatch, capture a concrete pinned-oracle source
   program, add a failing in-memory regression through the real interpreter,
   then fix its owning implementation. Cover subtype/explicit-descriptor paths,
   keywords, identity contracts, callback order and error precedence. Keep
   capabilities with their dedicated I/O/import implementations.
5. Extend behavioral evidence per entry and rerun the focused checks. Keep both
   `native-types` statuses open until every required API, service and behavior
   contract is verified; successful publication cannot close a row.

## Iterator exhaustion and callback edge audit — 2026-09-12

The original full CPython 3.14.7 compatibility task remains **open**. This
continuation adds behavior evidence and fixes one reproduced native exception
argument bug; it does not close the builtin inventory or certify complete
iterator compatibility.

### Reference and reproduction

The external oracle was `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, reporting CPython
3.14.7 (main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49), Clang 21.0.0,
Unicode 16.0.0, arm64, and `sys.maxsize == 9223372036854775807`.
The oracle executed the exact source programs now retained in
`packages/safe-python/src/runtime/__snapshots__/iterator-adversarial-3.14.7.json`.
Its 79 expected outputs are exact `repr(result)` captures, including exception
arguments, values, identity comparisons and callback event order. No output
normalization or process-dependent identities are involved.

The first 44 cases reproduced four failures: strict zip/map exhaustion after
resumable source errors produced `StopIteration.args == ('',)` instead of `()`.
Expanding to 79 cases before implementation reproduced **36 failures, 43 passes**.
All 32 additional native exhaustion probes also exposed `.value == ''` instead
of `None` and `repr(e) == "StopIteration('')"` instead of `StopIteration()`.
Both `next(r)` and `r.__next__()` were affected.

### Implementation and behavior evidence

`PythonRuntimeError` now retains the distinction between an omitted argument
message and an explicitly supplied empty string. Native exception preparation
uses that distinction when constructing guest args. The two native iterator
exhaustion paths now omit the message; explicit payloads remain intact. Existing
codec and key-error argument construction remains in its owning implementation.
No iteration algorithm or already-correct callback behavior was changed.

`src/session-iterator-adversarial.test.ts` executes all retained programs through
real `PythonSession` components, entirely in memory:

- Zip/map: strict and non-strict modes, StopIteration and ValueError at each of
  three source positions, exact input acquisition/pull order, exception identity,
  mismatch diagnostics, and retries from consumed positions.
- Zip/map strict truth conversion: zero through three positional arguments,
  successful conversion and callback failure, and exact error precedence.
- Resumable source exhaustion through filter(None), filter(bool), enumerate
  crossing the signed 64-bit index boundary, and direct iter.
- Repeated exhaustion and next defaults through list, tuple, string, range,
  dictionary, keys/values/items views, set, reversed list/tuple, zip, map, filter,
  enumerate and callable-sentinel iterators, via both public next call forms.
- Explicit StopIteration empty-string, None and nonempty payloads, including
  original exception identity through direct, zip, map, filter and enumerate.

## Native bytes construction and owned-method wiring — 2026-09-12

Status: **unfinished**. This does not close `codec-bytes-construction`,
`native-types`, or `codec-registry`. Their implement/test statuses are open.
The current work publishes an actual native bytes type, constructor, subtype
storage and existing method kernels through PythonSession. The complete buffer,
codec-registry, descriptor/introspection and traceback contracts remain required;
the missing components below are blockers, not compatibility exceptions.

### Implemented and reproduced

- `RuntimeTypeRegistry.bytesType()` owns canonical type publication, native
  allocation, variable-sized subtype layout, MRO and descriptors. PythonSession
  publishes that exact type; literals report it through `type`.
- Native allocation handles omitted input, counts, iterable byte indices,
  explicit buffer services, `__bytes__`, encoding/errors binding, signed-size
  overflow and native subtype allocation. `__bytes__` precedes `__index__`;
  TypeError during count conversion permits iterable fallback. Exact list
  collection observes mutation from item callbacks. Tuple and iterator/list
  single-byte identity policies differ as on the reference.
- Existing owned byte kernels are reached by actual bound/unbound descriptors,
  with metadata, class-bound `fromhex` and static `maketrans`. Subtype storage is
  accepted by the ordinary byte methods, arithmetic, comparisons, iteration,
  membership, slicing, hashing, representation and `str(bytes, encoding)`.
  No-op subtype copies canonicalize short bytes, ordinary nonempty copies have
  independent guest identities, partition retains its original receiver on a
  miss and its original separator on a hit, and reflected numeric methods run
  before native sequence fallback. Subtype repetition allocates even an empty
  result.
- Buffer construction requests an explicit full-readonly lease when supplied,
  copies its logical contents and releases it even if acquisition or copying
  triggers cancellation. Native immutable storage has an execution buffer
  adapter. **This is not a guest memoryview or complete PEP 688 implementation.**
- Encoded construction uses the same currently installed native encoding kernels
  as `str.encode`, retaining native encoding exceptions and argument validation.
  **It is not yet connected to a public per-interpreter codec registry.**
- Method documentation/signatures come from the pinned oracle. Staticmethod
  documentation and dictionary reflection now reach their existing native type
  descriptors; the static wrapper's documentation differs from the wrapped
  `maketrans` function's documentation.

All runtime changes are in `packages/safe-python`. No README, root CLI, commit,
push or release was changed/performed. Unit tests use in-memory values and
explicit buffer test services. Python runs only as an external development
oracle, never in runtime code or unit tests.

### Exact evidence

Reference: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython **3.14.7**,
`main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49`, Clang 21.0.0, `sys.platform == 'darwin'`,
`sys.maxsize == 9223372036854775807`, Unicode **16.0.0**. Inspected
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/bytesobject.c`,
particularly bytes_new_impl, PyBytes_FromObject, list/tuple/iterator collection,
concatenation and repetition. Native metadata is covered by CPYTHON-LICENSE.txt.

Mutation/copy and allocation-budget tests also pass. These are component/service tests, not public memoryview evidence. |

This does not verify the complete behavioral or inherited API inventory. |

### Required remaining work; no closure claim

1. Implement real memoryview/buffer objects and complete bytes `__buffer__`,
   PEP 688 acquisition/release, flags, strides/noncontiguous C-order copies,
   released views, exporter errors, mutable bytearray/native exporters,
   aliasing, pinning and cancellation through real public service adapters.
   Current public reproductions in separate fresh sessions:
   `b'a'.__buffer__(0)` raises AttributeError; `bytes(memoryview(b'abc')[::2])`
   and `bytes(bytearray([65]))` raise NameError. The native bytes buffer adapter
   currently inspects subtype storage directly and does **not** dispatch a
   subtype's guest `__buffer__` override. For example, the oracle calls
   `B.__buffer__(0)` for `b'ab'.strip(B(b'a'))`; a non-memoryview result raises
   `TypeError('__buffer__ returned non-memoryview object')`. This mismatch is
   unresolved and must not be accepted as a native fast path.
2. Wire bytes construction and every text consumer to the same real
   per-interpreter registry and registered handlers through public imports.
   PythonSession still lacks `__import__`, codecs/_codecs/encodings publication
   and guest registry access. Custom search, custom error handlers, codec-result
   subtypes, exceptions/notes/tracebacks and suspension have not been verified
   through public construction. Native kernel encoding alone does not satisfy
   this requirement.
3. Preserve actual codec callback contracts. The pinned oracle demonstrates
   `bytes(S('x'), 'custom')` and `S('x').encode('custom')` pass the original str
   subtype as their only argument when errors is omitted; explicitly supplying
   `'strict'` adds the second argument. Custom decoders called by bytes.decode
   and str(bytes, encoding) receive a **memoryview**, not a replacement bytes
   object. These dependencies prevent claiming shared-registry completion.
4. Finish native/inherited introspection and iterator/reduction APIs.
   `bytes.__basicsize__`, `bytes.__itemsize__`, `bytes.__flags__` currently raise
   AttributeError; `type(iter(b'a')).__name__` terminates for unavailable
   canonical iterator type; `b'a'.__reduce__()` raises AttributeError.
   Each reproduction used a fresh session after observing that a terminated
   PythonSession remains terminated. Results from reusing a terminated session
   were discarded rather than attributed to later expressions.
5. Finish full API-family behavioral matrices, including subtype buffer-slot
   overrides, allocation failure behavior, descriptor validation and rebinding,
   class mutation/layout metadata, serialization, warnings and exact traceback
   attributes. The 42 representative method rows and 126 metadata successes are
   **not** evidence that all bytes contracts are verified.

to `open`, preserving the rest of the existing plan. `codec-bytes-construction`

### Reproduced changes and exact behavioral evidence

The pinned [builtin implementation source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/bltinmodule.c)
and direct external oracle executions establish the expected outcomes retained
in the new JSON snapshots. Unit tests execute those exact source programs in
the real TypeScript interpreter; they never launch Python or mock interpreter
components.

- `builtin-sum.ts`: classify native str/bytes subtype payloads before accepting
  a start value, using the existing storage inspectors. Previously empty inputs
  returned the subtype start; nonempty inputs invoked its `__add__` override.
  CPython instead raises the family-specific TypeError after iterator
  acquisition and before consuming input or invoking addition. The new
  `session-sum-subtypes.test.ts` initially had **8 failures, 13 passes**. Its
  **21** oracle cases now pass: positional/keyword starts, empty/nonempty inputs,
  acquisition exceptions, invalid iterators, noniterable inputs, no conversion
  callbacks, plus retained arbitrary-start identity and ordinary rather than
  in-place addition.
- `builtin-ord.ts`: when no explicit byte-storage hook is supplied, inspect
  the real bytes subtype payload. Previously every tested bytes subtype raised
  the wrong unsupported-type error. `session-ord-bytes-subtypes.test.ts`
  initially had **5 failures** and now has **5 passes**. Empty/two-byte payloads
  produce exact length errors; ASCII, NUL and 0xff produce canonical integer
  values. Overridden `__len__`, `__bytes__`, `__str__`, `__index__`,
  `__getitem__` and `__buffer__` are not called. The buffer override in these
  programs must remain uncalled; these tests are not memoryview evidence.
  Explicit storage hooks retain their existing precedence.

No string method implementation changed. No I/O/import placeholder, ambient
capability, source substitution, backend delegation or reduced assertion was
introduced. Existing edits in the package and plan were preserved.

A further current-code reproduction identifies a reflective-builtin blocker:

```python
class Name(str): pass
class C:
 def __init__(self): self.x=1
# Evaluate each independently:
getattr(C(), Name('x'))
hasattr(C(), Name('x'))
setattr(C(), Name('x'), 2)
delattr(C(), Name('x'))
```

The oracle returns `1`, `True`, `None`, `None`. Fresh guest sessions raise
`TypeError("attribute name must be string, not 'instance'")` for all four.
`attribute-name.ts` lacks the default native subtype classification, and the
builtin invocation attribute interface currently converts names to host strings.
Fixing only validation would lose the guest name passed to override hooks;
complete repair must preserve CPython's original-name/lookup/descriptor contract
through the owning object protocols, with new failing tests first. This gap
remains unresolved, not an accepted restriction. Every other inventory entry
without complete behavioral evidence remains open as well.

## Bytes constructor descriptor and reservation continuation — 2026-09-12

Status: **unfinished**. The complete CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 bytes
contract remains required. This continuation does not close
`codec-bytes-construction`, `native-types`, or `codec-registry`. A fresh parsed
YAML audit found native-types marked done/done and bytes construction marked
open/done despite the remaining inventory failures. Changed only those three
status scalar spans to `open` using their YAML node ranges. Both codec registry
rows already remained open/open. Existing prompts and unrelated changes were
preserved.

The constructor is already registered in the current implementation. The
reported missing builtin no longer reproduces: the initial focused run of
`session-bytes.test.ts`, `session-bytes-binding`, and
`session-utf7-shift-boundaries` passed **203 tests in 3 files**. The retained
constructor/literal paths were left intact.

### Newly reproduced and repaired behavior

- **Writer reservation and identity:** all three new public-session programs in
  `session-bytes-writer-identity.test.ts` failed before the change and passed on
  the external oracle. CPython's release-build inline writer capacity is 512
  bytes. An iterator reservation above that capacity retains fresh nonempty
  output identity even if it yields only one byte. The previous implementation
  always canonicalized that byte. The constructor now retains the initial
  reservation when selecting result identity, including exact lists that shrink
  during element `__index__`, list subclasses using their source length, and
  original iterable length hints. Empty output remains canonical; exact tuple
  construction retains its existing fresh nonempty result policy. Initial list
  and tuple reservations are now charged before element conversion as well.
- **Index descriptor binding:** one of three new programs in
  `session-bytes-index-binding.test.ts` failed before the change. A `TypeError`
  raised while binding an input's `__index__` descriptor must permit the same
  iterable fallback as a `TypeError` raised when calling that method. Binding
  previously happened outside that fallback boundary. It now occurs inside it.
  `ValueError`, `AttributeError`, and `OverflowError` identity remain intact;
  `__bytes__` binding errors still propagate without index/iterable fallback.
- **Already-correct constructor argument precedence:** independently generated
  **700** oracle rows cover positional arguments, duplicate arguments, keyword
  order, unknown/suggested keywords, invalid encoding/errors types, lone
  surrogates and embedded NULs. All passed before any binder changes; the binder
  was left unchanged. The cases are retained in
  `runtime/__snapshots__/bytes-constructor-precedence-3.14.7.json` and exercised
  by `session-bytes-constructor-precedence.test.ts` through real guest calls.
- **Public cancellation/allocation evidence:** six in-memory tests in
  `session-bytes-cancellation.test.ts` pass. Cancellation arrives through the
  actual supported session output adapter while guest `__bytes__`, `__index__`,
  `__iter__`, `__len__`, or `__next__` executes. It terminates the session and
  cannot be caught as `BaseException`. A reservation exceeding the allocation
  budget terminates before advancing the iterator. These establish the sandbox
  budget/cancellation boundary, not complete CPython MemoryError or buffer
  lifecycle compatibility.

Reference source inspected: CPython v3.14.7 `Objects/bytesobject.c`, especially
`bytes_new_impl`, `_PyBytes_FromList`, `_PyBytes_FromTuple`,
`_PyBytes_FromIterator`, `_PyBytesWriter_Alloc` and `_PyBytesWriter_Finish`.
No host Python/eval is used by the runtime or unit tests.

   the existing guest length protocol and uses the existing containment policy
   when the selected target is a subtype. It preserves keyword/arity precedence,
   identity shortcuts and strict greater-than swapping.

## 2026-09-12 — dictionary-view rich comparison subtype audit

The complete CPython 3.14.7 compatibility objective remains **unfinished**.
The existing census (159 builtin names, 185 type paths, 6,415 member entries)
remains the inventory; this pass adds behavioral evidence for the six rich
comparison descriptors on `dict_keys`, `dict_items`, `set` and `frozenset`.
It does not certify every contract of those descriptors or any other census row.

Read the root AGENTS.md, current builtin assembly, type registry, native
comparison descriptors, dictionary-view kernels and prior evidence before
editing. Existing edits were preserved. The suspected distinction between
`round(x)` and `round(x, None)` for a custom `__round__` was disproved by the
pinned oracle: both call it without arguments. That implementation was left
unchanged.

### Reproduction and repairs

- Initial retained public-session matrix: **960 failed / 0 passed**. View base
  descriptors returned `NotImplemented` for set/frozenset subclasses, losing
  their length, containment and iteration callbacks. Operator paths likewise
  lost callbacks or returned incorrect results/errors.
- Added a native view comparison implementation that uses set payloads only to
  establish operand eligibility, then invokes existing runtime length,
  iteration and containment protocols on the original guest object. This
  preserves length validation, length-before-iteration order, inequality
  direction, containment truth conversion and callback exceptions.
- After that repair: **720 passed / 240 failed**. The remaining reflected
  expressions exposed a separate base-set-slot defect: its combined native
  kernel accepted dictionary views instead of declining them. The base slot
  now returns `NotImplemented` for non-set operands, allowing the view's
  reflected comparison to receive the original set subtype. A targeted
  reproduction independently failed all **24** explicit set/frozenset base
  descriptor cases before this second repair. The final suite runs all cases,
  without filtering or skipped tests.
- Reference: `dictview_richcompare` and `all_contained_in` in
  [CPython v3.14.7 dictobject.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/dictobject.c).

containment truth callbacks/failures, comparison overrides, unsupported operands,
keyword/arity/receiver validation, and explicit set base-slot decline.

Status: **unfinished, with a retained failing compatibility test**. The target
remains CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 on the pinned reference platform. Parsed
frontmatter confirms `native-types`, `codec-bytes-construction`, and
`codec-registry` remain open/open. No parent or constructor row is closed.

### Baseline, reproduced gaps, and implementation

Read the root AGENTS.md and current native bytes allocator, descriptors,
iteration, registry, invocation context, session tests, and prior plan evidence.
No package-specific AGENTS.md was present. The original `NameError` for bytes
still does not reproduce: the baseline focused run passed **48 files / 3,306
tests**, including all retained UTF-7 constructor and literal batches.

Four new public-session contracts first passed on the external oracle and
failed in the guest: `type(iter(b'abc'))` terminated because its canonical type
was unavailable, and iterator reduction/state methods raised AttributeError.
Implemented `RuntimeBytesIterator` and registered the native `bytes_iterator`
type. Its five own methods (`__iter__`, `__next__`, `__length_hint__`,
`__reduce__`, `__setstate__`) are real wrapper/method descriptors over the owned
cursor. Direct construction and subclassing are forbidden, as on CPython.
The cursor retains the original bytes subtype object for reduction; setting
its index to its length does not release the source until a subsequent next
observes exhaustion. Negative and oversized in-range states clamp; exhausted
cursors do not restart. State validation accepts native int/bool storage and
int subtype payloads, rejects arbitrary __index__ providers, and preserves the
signed Py_ssize_t overflow diagnostic.

Reduction obtains `iter` through an explicit active-frame builtin-namespace
service before reading cursor state. Reentrant guest dictionary lookup can
move the cursor, replace the builtin, or raise an existing guest exception.
No host objects or host evaluator implement guest behavior. `bytes.__iter__`
and exact-byte iteration now use this cursor. The registry's old test that
asserted bytes had no native type was reproduced as a failure and updated to
assert identity with `registry.bytesType()`; runtime bytes construction was
already correctly registered and was left intact.

Reference source: CPython v3.14.7 `Objects/bytesobject.c`, its `striter_next`,
`striter_reduce`, `striter_setstate`, and `PyBytesIter_Type` definitions:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/bytesobject.c
