## 2026-09-12 codec registry continuation: keyword subtype boundaries

Status: **unfinished**. This change does not complete codec-registry, any
encoding-family module, source/text I/O integration, or public import publication.
The existing bounded family tasks remain in this same pipeline; no duplicate
family tasks or substitute modules were introduced.

### Reproduction and implementation

Reading AGENTS.md, PythonSession, RuntimeCodecRegistry, its native bindings,
recovery adapters and the shared conversion argument binder confirmed that the
registry kernels exist but PythonSession does not install __import__ or publish
codecs/_codecs/encodings. Before editing, the public/core gate reproduced 31
failures: 28 missing-import failures and three missing UnicodeEncodeError
traceback assertions. These are implementation blockers, not accepted exceptions.

A separate external-oracle probe reproduced a conversion boundary mismatch:
str.encode and bytes.decode rejected str-subclass keyword names with
`TypeError('keywords must be strings')`. CPython accepts native Unicode storage
for keyword binding without invoking subclass equality or str. Its diagnostic
fallback subsequently compares every supplied key against parameter names with
Python equality, converts the comparison result to bool, and renders only the
first rejected key with str. This includes already-bound keys. If subclass
comparisons claim every key is accepted despite failed native binding, CPython
raises `TypeError('invalid keyword argument for encode()')` (or decode).

Changes in packages/safe-python:

- runtime-call.ts now accepts genuine str-subclass payloads at the generic
  call-site keyword boundary, preserving the original key objects.
- runtime-codec-arguments.ts binds names from native payloads and shares the
  complete unexpected-keyword diagnostic path with
  runtime-codec-registry-functions.ts. Suggestions use the original spelling;
  diagnostics use the guest-rendered spelling. Equality, truth and rendering
  failures propagate in order. Count, missing-argument and duplicate-argument
  precedence remain ahead of this diagnostic fallback.
- str.encode and bytes.decode supply their owning RuntimeValues to the binder.
- session-codec-keyword-subtypes.test.ts exercises actual public PythonSession
  conversions, duplicate binding, overridden equality/truth/rendering, exact
  exception messages and guest failure identity. Six cancellation scenarios
  use the real session output adapter and abort signal, covering encode/decode
  during equality, truth and rendering; termination remains permanent.
- runtime-codec-registry-functions.test.ts adds two compiled-guest binding
  regressions verifying that keyword diagnostics finish before codec lookup.
  Those bindings are not evidence of real public module publication.

No runtime code uses host Python, eval, host codecs, implicit filesystem access,
or host Unicode classification. Tests use in-memory interpreter state and no LLM.

### Reproduced changes and TDD

`session-builtin-keyword-subtypes.test.ts` initially ran 66 oracle programs:
**64 failed, 2 passed**. Native parsers rejected str-subclass keyword keys even
though call assembly accepted them. Repaired `min`, `max`, `pow`, `round`,
`sum`, `sorted`, and bound/explicit `list.sort` through their owning factories.
Known names use native Unicode payloads without invoking guest conversions or
equality. Arguments, key functions, defaults and return references remain guest
objects; no coercion or host capability was introduced.

Payload inspection alone left **40 failures**. CPython's leftover-keyword error
pass tests membership in the accepted-name tuple through rich equality, then
formats the original offending key using str. The new shared
`unexpected-builtin-keyword.ts` implements this diagnostic pass through explicit
invocation comparison/representation capabilities, including comparison truth
conversion, exception propagation, suggestions from the original payload, and
`invalid keyword argument for ...()` when all extraneous keys claim equality.
It runs only after the native binder detects leftovers. Missing-required,
position/name duplicate, total-count and iteration precedence stay with each
builtin's existing parser. Accepted names do not run diagnostic callbacks.

Expanded cases cover false/true/NotImplemented/nonboolean equality results,
raising equality, raising or invalid str results, unknown names, suggestions,
empty and non-ASCII names, key/reverse callbacks, materialization ordering,
mutation, default identity and explicit versus bound sort descriptors.

Seven further duplicate-payload cases all failed first. Distinct str-subclass
keys can have identical native text but compare unequal. Binders now retain the
first binding and send leftover entries through the diagnostic pass. The same
cases exposed an extra equality call while merging an exact dictionary into
empty keyword storage. `OrderedKeyMap.update` now directly inserts cached
entries when the same-domain source is a cloneable combined dictionary, without
rechecking equality between keys already present in that source.

A separate seven-case `session-dict-merge-callbacks.test.ts` reproduced **three
failures** at the clone boundary. `DictionaryEntrySlots` now retains capacity
and exposes the actual merge criterion: no deleted entry slots, and either
minimum table size or live entries exceeding the usable fraction of a
half-sized table. Pop-trimmed oversized tables and tables with holes take the
ordinary merge path. No equality/hash callbacks are removed from that path.
The cases assert exact callback sequences and both source/destination contents.
Full CPython hash-table layout/probing remains a blocker described below.

Sources checked directly:
[CPython keyword diagnostics and unpacking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/getargs.c),
[list.sort binding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/clinic/listobject.c.h),
[dictionary merge clone conditions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/dictobject.c).

### Exact evidence and unresolved hash-seed mismatch

The keyword snapshot retains all original 113 programs/expected outputs and
adds seven explicit guest-hash-17 duplicate cases, for **120** cases. No earlier
case or assertion was removed or weakened. Original capture used process-random
hashing; a fresh random-seed replay exposed variation in dictionary probe callback
counts, so those captures are not sufficient deterministic oracle evidence.
The seven additional programs specify their guest key hash and preserve exact
callback assertions; they do not replace the original programs.

To investigate rather than normalize away that variation, replayed **all 120**
programs under `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and real guest sessions with SipHash key
`[0n, 0n]`. `builtin-keyword-hash-seed-0-observations.json` retains every exact
oracle/guest result and reports **119 matches, 1 mismatch**. The mismatch is:

`pow(2, **{Keyword('exp'): 2, Keyword('exp'): 3})`, with str-subclass equality
logging and returning False. Both raise the same unexpected-keyword TypeError.
CPython logs `exp==exp` twice while constructing the keyword dictionary, then
`exp==base`, `exp==exp`, `exp==mod` during diagnostics. The guest logs the first
construction comparison only once. OrderedKeyMap's bucket scan does not model
CPython's perturbation probe sequence. This is concrete unresolved behavior,
not an allowed hash-randomization difference: the comparison used matched zero
hash secrets. It has not been turned into a compatibility pass or hidden by
filtering callback events. General collision/reentrancy schedules, clone layout,
split dictionaries and allocation behavior still require implementation/evidence.

Keyword snapshot SHA-256:
`b02588e678d5d10152a11cbfdab40c182f5432ec5b16f27b5f974192634bac4b`.
Seven mapping-merge oracle contracts independently replayed successfully with
hash seed zero; their snapshot SHA-256 is
`7777f4051c2df0424472e21c9a6e8b34704bc5c4135f6cb7bf14cf66bb13216e`.

### Reproduction and changes

The initial 34-case oracle suite failed **28** cases before runtime edits.
`builtin-print.ts` incorrectly required exact string keyword keys. It now binds
native Unicode payloads for str subclasses, preserves the first binding when
unequal keys share a payload, and routes leftover keywords through the existing
execution-owned rich-equality and string-rendering diagnostic pass. Accepted
keywords do not call their equality, str, iter or len overrides. Original values
and stream objects remain guest references. Print still owns binding and I/O
ordering; no stream capability was moved into the root CLI or acquired ambiently.

That repair left one failure in a `print(..., file=stream, **mapping)` call.
CPython's nonempty rejecting dictionary merge checks containment, then performs
an independent insertion lookup. OrderedKeyMap performed only one lookup.
Seven additional differential cases reproduced **six** further failures before
changing merge behavior. `OrderedKeyMap.update` now performs both lookups when a
rejecting merge starts nonempty. A match during containment rejects the key;
a match appearing only during insertion overwrites the existing value. A merge
starting empty retains CPython's ordinary override behavior and existing clone
path. Source values are captured before callbacks, and mutation checks occur
after insertion. The implementation does not synthesize callback events.

Cases cover all four accepted print keywords, subtype values, unknown/empty
names, suggestions, false/true/NotImplemented/nonboolean equality results,
raising equality, invalid/raising str, unequal keys with identical payloads,
changing equality answers between merge lookups, second-lookup exceptions,
source clearing/value mutation, flush truth/error precedence, and default values.
Twelve further stream cases verify partial writes, mutation/removal of methods,
lookup failures, noncallable write/flush, arbitrary write return values, false
flush, and separator conversion failures. Those twelve already matched and
required no runtime changes. Existing string methods were left intact.

Sources inspected:
[CPython print keyword wrapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/clinic/bltinmodule.c.h),
[print implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/bltinmodule.c),
[dict_dict_merge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/dictobject.c).

## 2026-09-12 additional guest attribute-name edge audit — unfinished

This continuation adds reproduction evidence, not a compatibility completion or
an implementation fix. The original scope and every earlier unresolved inventory
row remain required. No runtime code, README, CLI, commit, push or release was
changed by this continuation.

Reference: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, version `3.14.7 (main, Aug 5 2026,
10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`, Unicode `16.0.0`.
Python ran only as an external oracle. Each exact source and expected repr is
retained in `packages/safe-python/src/runtime/__snapshots__/attribute-edge-3.14.7.json`.
No Python process, eval delegation or host filesystem access was added to the
interpreter or unit tests.

### Reproduced behavior

`session-attribute-edge.test.ts` runs all 45 oracle programs through PythonSession,
without skips or expected-failure markers. It exercises getattr with/without a
default, hasattr, setattr and delattr using None, int, float, bytes, list, missing
plain-string names, empty names, embedded NUL names and str-subclass names whose
hash/equality calls are observable and whose str conversion raises.

Forty programs match. Five fail: every operation with `S('missing')` is rejected
as `TypeError: attribute name must be string, not 'instance'`, without callbacks.
CPython accepts that string subtype and records two `__hash__` callbacks in each
of these fresh-instance cases. Its results are:

| Operation | Oracle result before callback log |
| --- | --- |
| `getattr(x, name)` | AttributeError: `'C' object has no attribute 'missing'` |
| `getattr(x, name, 42)` | `42` |
| `hasattr(x, name)` | `False` |
| `setattr(x, name, 42)` | `None` |
| `delattr(x, name)` | AttributeError: `'C' object has no attribute 'missing'` |

These are active failing tests, not accepted compatibility differences. No
assertion was weakened and no failing case was removed. The focused check is
red and the task remains unfinished.

### Implementation inspection and required follow-through

The builtin attribute factories expose optional value-preserving contexts, but
the session path falls back to invocation capabilities accepting host `string`
names. Their validation lacks invocation-backed string-subtype classification.
`runtimeInstanceAttribute` and `runtimeMutateInstanceAttribute` recreate guest
keys with `values.string(name)`; object base descriptors also validate and then
convert their names to host strings. Merely accepting native string payloads
would lose observable name identity, hashing/equality, override arguments and
error precedence. No such partial workaround was installed.

The fix must carry original name objects through ordinary access, explicit base
descriptors, overrides and storage. It also needs evidence for class/metaclass,
native subtype/function dictionaries, descriptor precedence, hash/equality
failures and mutations, missing-attribute exception fields, and cancellation.
The two hash calls observed above are evidence for those exact programs, not a
license to synthesize two calls in an adapter. Actual lookup/storage operations
must produce the correct callback schedule. Relevant primary implementations:
[CPython object attributes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/object.c)
and [builtin dispatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/bltinmodule.c).

A separate suspected issue was disproved: CPython 3.14.7 accepts
`sorted([1,2], reverse=None)`, `reverse=1.1`, `reverse=[]`, and
`reverse=2**100`, returning respectively `[1,2]`, `[2,1]`, `[1,2]`, `[2,1]`.
An object providing both `__index__` and `__bool__` calls only `__bool__`.
The existing truth-conversion implementation was therefore left intact.

## 2026-09-12 bytes continuation: fromhex reservation identity and full retained replay

The requested bytes/native-types/codec-registry target remains **unfinished**.

### Reproduced and fixed behavior

An external CPython 3.14.7 probe found that fromhex identity depends on its
initial writer reservation, including whitespace, not only decoded output size:

- `bytes.fromhex('41' + ' ' * 1023)` returns the canonical single-byte object.
- `bytes.fromhex('41' + ' ' * 1024)` returns a fresh single-byte object on every
  call. Exact bytes inputs behave identically.
- Bytes heap-subtype fromhex construction receives that intermediate object's
  identity through its real `__new__` callback.

Captured **252** complete source programs and exact expected repr observations
in `runtime/__snapshots__/bytes-fromhex-reservation-3.14.7.json`. They cover seven
padding sizes; empty, one-byte and two-byte results; exact str/bytes and their
subtypes whose overridden `__len__` raises; class and bound-instance calls; and
heap-subtype construction observing intermediate inputs. The public-session
regression was red before runtime edits: **216 passed, 36 failed**. A separate
buffer-lease boundary regression was also red: **8 passed, 1 failed** in the
fromhex method file.

The native fromhex method now retains fresh result identity when
`floor(native input length / 2) > 512`, matching the pinned release writer's
inline capacity. Empty results remain canonical. Both native payload and buffer
export paths use their actual storage length; no guest length override is called.
The subtype constructor path receives the real result without special-casing
these tests. Parsing, validation, and release behavior remain in their existing
implementations. This follows the actual
[CPython bytes writer and fromhex implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/bytesobject.c).

Two additional suspicions were disproved and left unchanged: enormous iterable
integer elements raise ValueError for the byte range, and partition/rpartition
retain bytearray/memoryview separator objects in the middle result field on the
pinned interpreter. No speculative corrections were made for either behavior.

## Builtin inventory continuation: adversarial float.fromhex parsing

Status: **open / incomplete**. This continuation preserves the full CPython
3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 target; it does not certify the complete builtin inventory.
The native-types implementation status had returned to `done`; changed that
specific YAML scalar, located through its parsed AST, to `open`. Its test status
was already open. Other task statuses and unrelated edits were preserved.

### Reference and reproduced behavior

Rechecked `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14` as an external differential oracle:
`3.14.7 (main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49) [Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`,
`macOS-26.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O`, Unicode `16.0.0`.

The new retained snapshot,
`src/runtime/__snapshots__/float-fromhex-edge-cases-3.14.7.json`, records all
391 input literals and oracle outcomes, including exact exception classes,
messages and args. Successful outcomes retain `float.hex()` to expose signed
zero and binary64 rounding. NaN payload/sign-bit introspection is not certified
by these hexadecimal outcomes. The Python oracle only generated expectations;
unit tests execute the actual interpreter in memory without external Python.

The new public-session test `src/session-float-fromhex-edge-cases.test.ts`
initially reported **92 failed, 299 passed**. Two concrete faults were isolated
in `src/runtime/float-from-hex.ts`:

1. Special-value parsing truncated supplementary code points to UTF-16 code
   units. For example, `float.fromhex('i\U0001006ef')` produced infinity and
   `float.fromhex('n\U00010061n')` produced NaN, whereas CPython raises
   `ValueError: invalid hexadecimal floating-point string`. Special-value
   scanning now rejects non-ASCII points before conversion; its bounded word
   storage and existing ASCII spellings remain intact.
2. Trailing-text validation ran before numeric conversion. CPython raises
   `OverflowError: hexadecimal value too large to represent as a float` for
   both `1p1024x` and `0x1.fffffffffffff8p1023x`; the interpreter instead raised
   ValueError. Numeric conversion and rounding now precede trailing validation.
   Zero and underflow still validate trailing text, and the owning descriptor's
   existing strict UTF-8 conversion still runs first: `1p1024\ud800` raises
   UnicodeEncodeError. No encoding/string implementation was changed.

The 391 cases cover supplementary planes, signs and whitespace, malformed
special spellings and hex syntax, huge positive/negative exponents, embedded
NULs, surrogates, rounding-induced overflow, ties and sticky tails at normal and
subnormal boundaries, and 100 deterministically seeded significand/exponent
samples. Each case runs direct float construction, float-subclass construction
with a str-subclass input, and explicit classmethod-descriptor binding. Tests
check result types and `__new__`/`__init__` order; errors must occur before those
callbacks. This gives 1,173 conversion paths after the fixes, not 1,173 distinct
oracle inputs. No retained assertions or cases were weakened or excluded.

The existing `builtin-member-publication-audit.json` float.fromhex row now links
to these additional behavior tests without replacing its earlier evidence or
changing its partial classification. Python's 3.14 branch implementation was
also inspected for conversion-before-trailing-text ordering in
[Objects/floatobject.c](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.14/Objects/floatobject.c).
That moving source is corroboration, not the pinned 3.14.7 oracle.

Replayed all 159 retained builtin-name probes against the current public
session: **122 published, 37 missing**, with exactly the missing names recorded

### Reproduced blockers retained as failing tests

- Nine union construction cases fail: direct/bound Union.__or__/__ror__ with
  an ordinary instance or integer 0 should construct a union, and u|other
  should construct that union without invoking other's __ror__. The current
  shared eligibility check declines these operands and changes dispatch.
- Eight cases fail because list[int] raises "type 'list' is not subscriptable"
  before descriptor execution. Canonical GenericAlias construction is required.
- Inspected pinned CPython `Objects/unionobject.c`: `union_nb_or` uses checked
  construction and calls typing._type_check for non-unionable objects;
  `_Py_union_type_or` checks eligibility and uses unchecked construction.
  Simply removing eligibility checks would bypass required typing behavior
  (including forward references and invalid typing arguments). No such partial
  runtime substitute was introduced. The dedicated typing/import components
  and generic aliases remain necessary to implement the complete contract.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/unionobject.c
- Revalidated all five attribute-name subtype failures in session-attribute-edge
  and the exception traceback failure in session-bytes-iterator. They still fail.
- The earlier missing builtin/type/member inventory, bytearray/memoryview/buffer
  contracts, collection iterator types, full reflection, exception families,
  annotation behavior and real I/O/import adapter evidence remain open. This
  continuation does not rerun or certify the full publication inventory.

### Reproduced behavior fixes

1. Dictionary keys views backed by dict subtypes incorrectly borrowed cached
   hashes when converted to sets by union, difference and symmetric difference.
   CPython borrows hashes only for exact dictionaries. The first **240** retained
   oracle programs failed **45 / passed 195** before changing runtime code.
   `runtime-dictionary-view-algebra.ts` now respects the view's native owner.
   Subtype-backed conversion iterates native view storage, rehashes keys, and
   preserves callback failures and mutation detection without calling overridden
   dictionary keys/iteration methods. Exact dictionaries retain their fast path.
   The suspected set-subtype intersection optimization was checked against the
   pinned source and found correct; it was left intact.

   explicit guest TypeError from __hash__. An independent **225**-program
   hash/dictionary/set corpus reproduced **63** failures before the shared fix.
   Runtime hash provenance now retains guest exceptions, with exact native
   TypeError classification and deferred str rendering owned by exception
   execution. Container diagnostics render only where CPython does. TypeError
   subclasses and other exceptions propagate unchanged. hash(), tuple hashing,
   set intersection and subset paths retain original exception identity and
   arguments without rendering them. Internal hash provenance is unwrapped at
   exception preparation if no container consumes it. Rendering errors propagate
   with the observed context/cause behavior.
3. A subsequent qualified-name probe reproduced `K` instead of `custom.Outer.K`
   in contextual hash errors. Added **135** programs before changing name handling:
   **90 failed**, while all hash() controls retained their original exceptions.
   Diagnostic names are now deferred until needed and use native live metadata,
   bypassing metaclass __getattribute__. The existing qualified-name helper now
   reads string-subtype module payloads. Cases cover module/qualname mutation
   during hashing, non-string modules, empty modules, names longer than 200
   characters, NULs and lone surrogates. No string method was changed.

`runtime/__snapshots__/dict-view-native-conversion-3.14.7.json` (**400 programs**),

## 2026-09-12 bytes continuation: reconstruction argument identity

Status: **open / incomplete**. The target remains CPython 3.14.7, Unicode
16.0.0, on the pinned reference platform. Read AGENTS.md and the existing native
registry, constructor, descriptors and retained session tests before editing.
The original `NameError` for bytes no longer reproduces. This continuation does
not close bytes-construction, native-types or codec-registry.

### Reproduced defect and implementation

The native `bytes.__getnewargs__` descriptor returned the exact bytes receiver
inside its reconstruction tuple. CPython constructs an exact bytes result from
native storage, even for an exact receiver. Empty and one-byte results use the
canonical objects; longer results have distinct identities on successive calls.
A fresh one-byte source from `bytes(1)` or `bytes((97,))` must also be replaced by
the canonical byte in the reconstruction tuple.

Added `src/session-bytes-getnewargs-identity.test.ts` first. After correcting its
required session-limit configuration, the unchanged runtime failed its identity
assertions with `AssertionError()`. The identical guest source passed the live
external oracle. Changed only the reconstruction-result expression in
`runtime/runtime-bytes-descriptors.ts`, with an explanatory comment. The real
native descriptor now creates the canonical-or-fresh exact bytes wrapper through
the existing value owner. Immutable internal storage can be shared safely;
mutable guest storage or subtype dictionaries are not shared with the result.
The regression covers exact bytes, ordinary and slotted subtypes, empty/one-byte/
long values, repeated calls, constructor-created fresh single bytes, reconstruction
through `bytes(*args)`, and bypass of subtype conversion/iteration/length overrides.
It passes after the change. Other constructor and descriptor behavior was left
intact; this is not a replacement constructor or a literal rewrite.

Pinned implementation consulted:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/bytesobject.c
(`bytes_getnewargs`, using the native bytes buffer to build its tuple).

### Reproduced behavior and changes

Added `src/session-set-union-cached-hash.test.ts` and its independent external
oracle corpus, `src/runtime/__snapshots__/set-union-cached-hash-3.14.7.json`, before
changing runtime code. The first run exhausted the test fixture's 100,000-step
allowance; with the ordinary 2,000,000-step session allowance the unchanged
runtime produced **182 passes / 10 failures / 192 cases**. These ten failures
invoked a metaclass equality callback and raised `ValueError('comparison')`
where CPython returned False/True without invoking any callback.

CPython's frozenset equality rejects unequal already-cached hashes after its
size check. Union equality uses that same frozenset comparison for its hashable
arguments. Added `OrderedKeyMap.hasEqualKeys` and routed native set/frozenset
and union equality through it. It consults cached hashes only within the same
key-policy domain and never computes new hashes during comparison. Ordinary
subset comparisons, one-sided/absent hash caches, equal cached hashes, element
exception propagation and subtype overrides retain their existing behavior.

The **192 cases now pass**. They cover exact frozensets, frozenset subtypes and
unions; neither/left/right/both cached hashes; matching/distinct hashes;
all six comparison operators; explicit base `__eq__`/`__ne__` descriptors;
and callback order/errors versus subtype overrides. This is evidence for the
specified comparison behavior, not complete union or frozenset certification.
Linked partial evidence to **14 existing member rows** in
`builtin-member-publication-audit.json`, preserving previous evidence.

Reference implementations consulted:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/setobject.c
(`set_richcompare`) and
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/unionobject.c
(`unions_equal`). No string runtime methods were changed.

## 2026-09-12 — Native `dict.fromkeys` mutation and descriptor continuation

The original native-types task remains open. Its YAML `implement` status was
corrected from `done` to `open` through the YAML document parser; `test` remains
`open`. This is not completion of the builtin/member inventory or acceptance of
any compatibility exception. Existing evidence and unrelated work are retained.

### Reproduction and implementation

Read the repository instructions, builtin registration/type registry, native
fromkeys descriptor, ordered storage and dictionary entry-slot implementation.
Reproduced the bytes keyword reentrancy failure first:
`npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- session-bytes-keyword-subtypes`
reported **131 passed / 1 failed**. The `source mutation replace` case still
terminates with host `Maximum call stack size exceeded` instead of the oracle's
guest RecursionError. No host-error conversion or artificial recursion cutoff
was added; preserving guest recursion depth, side effects and traceback frames
remains required.

New native-fromkeys oracle programs exposed these additional gaps before fixes:

- Initial **24 cases: 7 passed / 17 failed**. Reentrant equality could clear,
  delete, append or refill source keys. The shared dictionary-update path raised
  `RuntimeError('dict mutated during update')`, while the reference completed.
  Even same-size clear/refill visited the wrong keys because a host entry cursor
  did not retain CPython's numeric dictionary entry position.
- After introducing native positional traversal, **35 cases: 34 passed / 1
  failed**. A self-source with a deleted entry hole, cleared and refilled with
  three keys during equality, failed to overwrite the third refill value. The
  reference compacts destination entries before traversing, including when the
  destination is the source itself.
- The canonical/inherited descriptor probe failed because
  `dict.__dict__['fromkeys'].__text_signature__` and its bound forms returned None
  instead of `($type, iterable, value=None, /)`.

`builtin-dictionary-fromkeys.ts` now sends exact dictionary sources to
`OrderedKeyMap.assignKeys`. That operation retains cached hashes, captures the
current key before callbacks, preserves destination key/value identity and
resumes using the current dictionary table at the saved numeric position.
`DictionaryEntrySlots.prepareFromKeys` reserves the native construction capacity
and compacts holes before traversal, retaining general-key layouts. The canonical
classmethod descriptor now publishes its observed text signature. Dictionary
update/keyword merging and the existing set/frozenset fromkeys path retain their
previous behavior; set-table traversal is not certified by this correction.

Reference implementation reviewed:
[CPython v3.14.7 `Objects/dictobject.c`](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.7/Objects/dictobject.c),
`_PyDict_FromKeys`, `dict_dict_fromkeys` and `dictresize`. No host Python or host
eval is used by the runtime implementation.

## 2026-09-12 — Canonical range iterator and state descriptor continuation

Status: **open / incomplete** under the same CPython 3.14.7, Unicode 16.0.0,
macOS arm64 target. Root AGENTS.md, builtin assembly, type registry, native
attributes, iteration and existing inventory evidence were read before changes.
The native-types YAML task was open/done; its test status is now open, changed
through the YAML parser's scalar range. Neither publication nor a partial
behavior corpus completes this task. Unrelated edits are retained.

### Reproduction and implementation

The original range adapter yielded integers but had no canonical guest cursor
type or native state/reduction descriptors. Created the independent external
oracle snapshot and public-session tests first. The initial **160 cases all
failed** against the unchanged runtime (including canonical iterator publication
termination and missing reduction). No string method implementation was changed.

`RuntimeRangeIterator` now owns the current start, step and remaining length.
Both `range_iterator` and `longrange_iterator` are canonically published with
real `__iter__`, `__next__`, `__length_hint__`, `__reduce__` and `__setstate__`
descriptors. Forward/reverse creation checks the original bounds, cardinality
and CPython's conservative LP64 overflow conditions. Empty reverse cursors
retain the reversed progression's start. State advances relative to the
remaining progression; it never rewinds an exhausted cursor. Fast cursors use
the integer-index protocol and C-long overflow checking; long cursors require
an exact int and retain arbitrary precision. Subtype payloads, conversion side
effects and qualified rejection diagnostics are covered by the reference cases.

Reduction constructs its range before resolving `iter` from the active builtin
namespace, preserving that snapshot through reentrant lookup. Long cursor
payload sharing is retained where the reference exposes it. All range creation
routes use the cursor, including `iter`, `reversed` and explicit range base
methods. No host Python, host eval, ambient output, filesystem or import
capability is used by the implementation.

Expanding the corpus reproduced **six additional guest failures**: five
cross-layout descriptors incorrectly named their rejected receiver `iterator`,
and native attribute mutation terminated at an unavailable capability. Trusted
cursor type-name metadata now survives iterator wrapping and descriptor
receiver diagnostics. Native default attribute mutation honors the canonical
layout's lack of an instance dictionary after consulting data descriptors,
producing the reference missing-attribute/read-only errors. Both default and
explicit object setters/deleters, immutable type mutation, keywords and receiver
precedence are exercised.

A focused integration test also failed because its fixed 344-byte allocation
allowance encoded the removed adapter's allocation total. Replaced that brittle
threshold with a meter which rejects allocation on the first pull, retaining
the allocation failure assertion and adding unchanged-length/first-value
assertions after rejection. The cancellation fixture initially omitted the
required hash seed; supplied it without changing its fatal-cancellation or
no-recovery assertions. All **185 oracle cases plus two cancellation tests**
now pass.

Reference source reviewed: [CPython v3.14.7 rangeobject.c](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/rangeobject.c),
including both iteration constructors, next/length/reduce/setstate implementations
and type/method declarations. This continuation does not certify the inherited
object methods or the full native layout model.

## 2026-09-12 continuation: string containment subtype dispatch

The complete CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 target remains unchanged and
unfinished. Read the repository instructions, existing inventory and current
builtin/type/descriptor implementations before editing. Preserved unrelated
working-tree edits. This continuation makes no README, CLI, commit or release
changes.

### Reproduced failures and correction

A public `PythonSession` program defining `class Text(str)` and evaluating
`Text('a') in 'abc'` raised a guest exception. The native expression membership
kernel rejected every non-exact string needle, although the explicit
`str.__contains__` descriptor already extracted subtype payloads. New tests also
reproduced incorrect invalid-needle type names in both operator and descriptor
calls. The initial six-test run had four behavioral failures and one execution
budget failure; the already-correct descriptor payload case exceeded the test
fixture's 100,000-step allowance. The final fixture allows 1,000,000 steps;
all assertions and all cases remain present.

`runtime-membership.ts` now reads the native string payload for either exact
strings or subtypes. Invalid needles use actual native type metadata and
CPython's 100-byte UTF-8 diagnostic-name precision. `runtime-string-slots.ts`
passes the original needle and invocation context to that shared implementation.
String conversion, equality and iteration overrides are not invoked to read a
needle's native payload. Ordinary receiver `__contains__` overrides still run;
explicit `str.__contains__` reads base storage.

Reference implementation inspected:
[CPython v3.14.7 PyUnicode_Contains](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/unicodeobject.c).
`string-containment-subtypes-3.14.7.json` retains eight executable programs:
operator `in`/`not in`, explicit base descriptors, exact/subtype haystacks,
empty/overlong/non-BMP/lone-surrogate needles, conversion/equality/iteration
tripwires, invalid operand classes, receiver override dispatch, and ASCII or
multibyte diagnostic names at the 100-byte boundary. Every program passes the
live `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14` oracle and public interpreter session. These
are bounded behavior checks, not certification of every string member or every
binding/introspection contract.

before the runtime edit. For `class B(bytes): pass`, `B(b'').partition(b'A')`

exact separator. `rpartition` had the corresponding failures.

objects can occupy other positions. The implementation now recognizes the
unmatched case by the empty middle component and preserves the subtype only at

kernel's separator and side identities. No constructor/literal rewriting or

### Reproduced input correction

CPython's noninteractive input path clears stdout.flush exceptions before
readline, including BaseException subclasses, while retaining prompt-write and
read failures. Primary implementation reference:

Before the runtime change, builtin-input.test.ts produced **10 failures / 22
passes**. Both native PythonRuntimeError and real RuntimeRaisedException carriers
for ValueError, TypeError, MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit escaped
flush instead of proceeding to read. builtin-input.ts now clears those guest
flush errors through the execution-owned exception classifier. Host errors and

The original bytes task remains **unfinished**. This correction preserves an

### Reproduced behavior and correction

CPython 3.14.7 calls a registered text codec with one positional argument when
`errors` is omitted, and with two when a policy is explicit. This applies to
`bytes(text, encoding)`, `text.encode(encoding)`, `str(data, encoding)` and
`data.decode(encoding)`. A codec accepting `*args` observes `()`, `('strict',)`
and `('ignore',)` for the three tested forms. The initial implementation
unconditionally supplied `strict`, overriding codec defaults and changing
argument-count errors.

Added an in-memory compiled-guest regression in runtime-codec-guest.test.ts
before editing runtime code: **1 failed / 6 passed**. The new test executes all
four real consumer kernels through RuntimeCodecRegistry and compiled guest
search/encode/decode functions, with twelve omitted/explicit/keyword calls.
It now passes. These fixture entry points are unit integration evidence only;
they do not substitute for the public-session failures below.

RuntimeTextEncoder, RuntimeTextDecoder and the string construction decoding
boundary now preserve undefined for omitted policies. The bytes/str constructors
and shared method argument binder retain the omission after validating provided
arguments. Native encoders and decoders apply strict handling locally; their
extension callbacks receive the original optional policy. No registry bypass,
host Python execution, source rewrite, dummy module or guest-data injection was
added to the runtime.

Two old unit expectations asserted an explicitly supplied strict argument for
omission. They now assert the oracle-confirmed missing argument. The compiled
invalid-result codec now declares its strict default, preserving every existing
result-error, cause/context, note and dispatch-event assertion. No failing
compatibility assertion was excluded or weakened.

## Dictionary positional cursor continuation — 2026-09-12

The complete CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 target remains **unfinished**.
This entry adds behavioral evidence and fixes reproduced dictionary traversal
mismatches; it does not close native iterator publication or the builtin inventory.
The prior inventory and all unresolved rows remain in force.

### Reproduction and implementation

Read repository AGENTS.md, the current builtin/type publication paths,
ordered-key-map.ts, both linked-order iterator kernels, dictionary-entry-slots.ts
and the existing dictionary evidence before changing code. Rechecked the pinned
external interpreter: CPython 3.14.7, Unicode 16.0.0, macOS 26.4.1 arm64,
64-bit non-free-threaded build. Reference source:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/dictobject.c,
particularly dictiter_iternextkey_lock_held, dictreviter_iter_lock_held and
dictiter_len. Python was used only as an external oracle, never by the runtime.

Added session-dictionary-cursor-mutation.test.ts and the retained reference
runtime/__snapshots__/dictionary-cursor-mutation-3.14.7.json **before** runtime
changes. Initial result: **452 passed / 140 failed / 592 total / zero skips**.
The old cursors followed host insertion order or predecessor links; this differed
from the reference's retained numeric table position after same-size mutation.
Concrete examples:

- After consuming the sole key, popitem followed by replacement leaves the
  forward cursor past the new table end. CPython raises StopIteration; the old
  cursor instead found the replacement and raised "dictionary keys changed
  during iteration".
- A reverse iterator over two keys, cleared and refilled with keys 100 and 101
  before consumption, must yield 101 then 100. The old linked cursor exhausted.
- Deletion holes, insertion-capacity exhaustion and exact-string-to-general
  conversion alter which entries a retained position encounters. A reverse
  position beyond a compacted table exhausts; it must not clamp to the new tail.

Implementation lives entirely in packages/safe-python/src/runtime:

- dictionary-storage-iterator.ts owns the numeric cursor, captured size,
  remaining count, sticky size errors, forward-only unexpected-key error and
  exhaustion. It resolves current storage for each next(), observes live values,
  advances before trusted item projection and retains the dictionary after a
  sticky size error, as the reference does.
- dictionary-entry-slots.ts exposes its last position and a budgeted backward
  scan which skips holes and rejects out-of-table retained positions.
- ordered-key-map.ts routes maps with dictionary positional storage through the
  new cursor. Existing non-positional/set kernels retain their existing behavior.
  The new scanner shares the existing allocation/layout rules; it does not add
  an independent approximation of compaction thresholds.
- Length hints preserve the reference's unsigned 64-bit size_t conversion,
  including negative remaining counts after reverse traversal repeats entries
  following compaction. No result normalization removes that observation.

The original 592 cases passed after the fix. Expanded to **712 cases**, adding
literal, comprehension, constructor and dictionary-subclass construction,
explicit dict.__iter__/dict.__reversed__, deletion holes and multiple consumed
positions. All **712 passed**, with no skipped or weakened assertions. The corpus
covers dictionaries plus keys/values/items views in both directions; first/last
replacement, popitem replacement, clear/refill, live value updates, observed
size errors followed by restoration, Unicode-layout conversion, compaction,
length hints after each step and repeated exhaustion after later mutation.
It compares yielded values, error type/message/args and retained observations.
It does not certify exception traceback objects or iterator identity/lifetime.

## 2026-09-12 callable iterator publication and native subclass hook

Status: **unfinished**. The original CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 target
and every earlier unresolved inventory item remain required. No compatibility
exception, unavailable-service exemption, skipped case, or reduced corpus is
introduced. This continuation does not certify all builtin behavior.

### Reproductions and implementation

- Callable-sentinel iterators had an execution engine but no canonical native
  type. The first 59 public-session descriptor cases failed; publication
  terminated with `canonical type for iterator is unavailable`. Added the
  execution-owned `callable_iterator` layout and its complete owned member set:
  `__doc__`, `__iter__`, `__next__`, and `__reduce__`. Native attribute dispatch
  now binds those descriptors. No constructor, subclassability, instance
  dictionary, or advisory length hint is fabricated.
- Reduction resolves `iter` in the calling frame's builtin namespace before
  inspecting cursor state. Reentrant lookup can exhaust the cursor; the result
  then uses `(iter, ((),))`. Active reduction retains the callable and sentinel
  by identity in fresh outer/argument tuples. Callable StopIteration releases
  state; equality StopIteration preserves the original exception and allows a
  later retry. Existing comparison/reentrancy behavior was retained.
- All initial 104 subclass-hook cases failed against the missing
  `object.__subclasshook__` descriptor. Installed the native class-method
  descriptor with CPython 3.14.7's **exactly one positional argument** contract,
  keyword rejection, dynamic receiver qualified-name diagnostics, and defining
  owner metadata. The successful return is the canonical NotImplemented object,
  as required by CPython's actual `object_subclasshook` implementation; this is
  not a placeholder for ABCMeta behavior. The argument is deliberately not
  inspected. Guest overrides and explicit base-descriptor calls remain distinct.
- The subclass-hook metadata case reproduced an AttributeError for bound
  builtin `__module__`. Implemented the canonical writable member descriptor
  and per-callable weak storage. Values retain identity, accept arbitrary guest
  objects, and deletion returns subsequent reads to None. Initial module strings
  are cached, and separately retrieved bound methods have independent module
  storage. Public-session builtin publication supplies its actual builtin module
  name. A further probe reproduced missing `len.__name__`; unbound native
  callable names/qualified names no longer depend on whether the factory
  supplied module metadata.
- The override case reproduced an extra metaclass `__getattribute__('__new__')`
  callback during native allocation. Native tp_new wrappers now bypass ordinary
  metaclass lookup; Python-defined allocators and explicit staticmethod wrappers
  still use it. Native allocator selection and explicit __new__ safety checks
  remain in the existing allocation implementation.

Primary implementation references, checked against the pinned version:

- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/iterobject.c
  (`calliter_iternext`, `calliter_reduce`, `PyCallIter_Type`).
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/typeobject.c
  (`object_subclasshook`, its METH_CLASS | METH_O registration, `slot_tp_new`,
  and the native tp_new special case in slot updates).

Disproved suspicions were left unchanged: longrange_iterator.__setstate__ really
rejects bool and int subtypes; ordinary range_iterator accepts their integer
payloads. The examined object.__dir__ dictionary-subtype override and sequence
cases also matched the pinned oracle. No string implementation was changed.

## Builtin edge audit continuation: numeric sum phases (2026-09-12)

The original CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 target remains unchanged. This
continuation does not close the builtin inventory or certify complete behavior
of `sum`. Existing inventory rows and unresolved requirements remain mandatory.

### Reproduced defect and implementation

External reference: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`, CPython 3.14.7
(main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49), Clang 21.0.0, Darwin arm64, Unicode 16.0.0.
Source cross-check:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/bltinmodule.c
(`builtin_sum_impl`, float and complex accumulator branches).

`src/runtime/sum-iterator.ts` used only exact integer/Boolean operands in its
float and complex phases, and only exact floats in its complex phase. Numeric
subclasses therefore left compensated accumulation for ordinary addition.
Ordinary addition often produced the correct immediate value, but lost the
compensation needed by subsequent operands. For example, with `class I(int)`:
`sum([1e16, I(1), -1e16], 0.0)` must produce `1.0`, not `0.0`. The analogous
complex accumulation must retain its real compensation for both integer and
float subclasses.

The fix uses the existing pure native integer/float payload readers in precisely
those phases. It does not invoke guest conversion hooks or change exact-type
requirements on phase entry, integer accumulation, float operands in the float
phase, or complex operands in the complex phase. Generic addition remains generic
once reached. No new runtime services, host Python delegation, source rewriting,
placeholder APIs, or ambient capabilities were introduced.

## 2026-09-12 codec error-handler return validation order

This continuation fixes one reproduced registry mismatch. It does **not** close
codec-registry or its integration/family rows. The complete CPython 3.14.7,
Unicode 16.0.0 target and all prior unresolved requirements remain in force.

### Evidence and correction

Read repository AGENTS.md, current registry/bindings/recovery, public import gates,
source/text consumers and existing bounded codec pipeline rows before editing.
Reference oracle: /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 reports CPython 3.14.7
(main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49), Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101),
Unicode 16.0.0. Python was used only as an external oracle.

Pinned source inspected:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Objects/unicodeobject.c
(unicode_encode_call_errorhandler and unicode_decode_call_errorhandler_writer)
and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.7/Python/codecs.c.
Encoding parses the handler tuple as (object, Py_ssize_t), then validates the
replacement. Decoding parses it as (str, Py_ssize_t), validating the replacement
before invoking a position's __index__. The shared registry previously rejected
invalid encoding replacements before __index__, suppressing observable guest
mutation/failure and choosing the wrong exception.

External oracle: 20 cases across ascii_encode, latin_1_encode, utf_8_encode,
ascii_decode and utf_8_decode. Handler returns (None, Position()); __index__ records
'index' and either returns -1, raises a retained ValueError('position failed'),
returns 1 << 63, or returns 'bad'. All three encoders call __index__ first:

| Position outcome | Exact exception and args |
| --- | --- |
| -1 | TypeError('encoding error handler must return (str/bytes, int) tuple') |
| retained failure | the same ValueError('position failed') instance |
| 1 << 63 | OverflowError('Python int too large to convert to C ssize_t') |
| 'bad' | TypeError('__index__ returned non-int (type str)') |

Both decoders leave events empty for all four modes and raise
TypeError('decoding error handler must return (str, int) tuple'). Another 15
external oracle cases confirm malformed tuple/list results fail before invoking
Position.__index__. No result or failure was normalized away.

TDD: added five compiled-guest parameterized cases to
src/runtime/runtime-core-codec-functions.test.ts. Before the runtime change the
three encoding cases failed and both decoding cases passed. The same run also
reproduced three missing-traceback failures in existing rejected-replacement
checks. Changed only the shared validation sequence in runtime-codec-registry.ts:
tuple shape first; decoding replacement type before position; encoding replacement
type after index conversion and signed-size overflow validation, before bounds.
Added malformed-result checks and two cancellation checks where __index__ cancels
then returns or raises. They exercise real compiled guest methods, exceptions,
registry and codec kernels, without public-module substitutes or host execution.

- Final focused run: **842 passed, 3 failed**, 16 files, 6.09 seconds.
  Command: npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- runtime-codec-registry runtime-core-codec-functions runtime-codec-handler-guest runtime-codec-guest runtime-codec-dispatch runtime-wide-codec-guest runtime-codec-errors utf8-incremental utf8-signature utf-wide runtime-text-codec-result --reporter=dot.
  All eight newly added tests pass. The three remaining failures are the ASCII,
  Latin-1 and UTF-8 rejected-replacement assertions that error.__traceback__ is
  not None. RuntimeExceptionExecution currently does not attach guest tracebacks

## 2026-09-12 codec edge-case audit: UTF-7 recovery and public gates

Status: **unfinished**. This audit does not close `codec-registry`,
`codec-registry-integration`, or any encoding-family row. Their existing bounded
pipeline tasks and the full CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 completion requirement
remain unchanged. No runtime behavior was changed without a reproduced mismatch.

Read root AGENTS.md, the existing codec pipeline and latest evidence, registry,
core bindings/recovery, standard error handlers, UTF-8/signature/wide incremental
kernels, UTF-7 and exception/traceback machinery. No nested AGENTS.md was found
under packages/safe-python. Preserved unrelated working-tree edits.

### Executed checks and exact evidence

- `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- codec utf8-incremental utf8-signature utf-wide source-encoding --reporter=dot`:
  **7,440 passed, 31 failed**, 28 files, 9.10 seconds. The eight public import
  gates fail with `ImportError('__import__ not found')`; 20 public codec-contract
  cases fail; three ASCII/Latin-1/UTF-8 rejected-replacement cases fail because
  `error.__traceback__ is None`. Assertions were retained without skips or
  normalization. These failures remain required implementation work.
- External oracle `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14`: CPython **3.14.7**
  `(main, Aug 5 2026, 10:29:49)`, Clang 21.0.0, Unicode **16.0.0**.
  Python was used only for differential evidence, never runtime implementation.
- Ran an in-memory **12,000-case UTF-7 differential audit**, with **zero
  mismatches**. Reproduction: initialize Python `random.Random(7147)`; for each
  case draw a byte length with `randrange(1,19)`, draw bytes from
  `b'+-ABCDEF0123/!\xff\x80'`, choose errors from strict, ignore, replace,
  backslashreplace, surrogatepass, surrogateescape, and choose final from
  `[True, False]`. Compare `codecs.utf_7_decode` with the real `decodeUtf7`
  kernel. Compare output code points and consumed count, or exact encoding,
  input bytes, start, end and reason. Oracle JSON was piped directly to a
  Node/tsx comparison process; no temporary test files or host runtime codec
  delegation were introduced. This finite audit is not exhaustive compatibility
  proof and does not satisfy public module/service verification.
- Checked standard error-handler empty-object ranges for encode/decode/translate
  at `(0,0)`, `(1,1)`, `(-1,-1)` and `(9,0)` against the oracle. Their current
  behavior agrees; retained it. Inspected the oracle's UTF-16/32 incremental
  decoder state implementation; its integer-state selection agrees with the
  existing kernel.
- Added two parameterized tests (eight recovery scenarios) to
  `packages/safe-python/src/runtime/utf7.test.ts`. Original inputs have lengths
  1 and 7, starting with `0xff`; the first handler replaces input with `+A`,
  `AB+A`, `+2AA` or `ABC+A`, returning empty text and position zero. The second
  error has the replacement object and shift-start offset, but its EOF end
  remains **the original input length**, even when end is less than start or
  exceeds the replacement length. A second replacement of `?` resumes at the
  replacement length; outputs are `?`, `AB?`, `?`, `ABC?`, with consumed counts
  1 or 7 respectively. All eight match the pinned oracle. Current kernel
  behavior was already correct, so no runtime edit was appropriate.
- `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- utf7 --reporter=dot`:
  **83 passed**, 3 files, 20.06 seconds; no failures or skips.
- `npm run typecheck --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python`: passed.

## 2026-09-12 public native codec module bootstrap (unfinished)

The requested complete CPython 3.14.7 / Unicode 16.0.0 registry remains
**unfinished**. `codec-registry`, `codec-registry-integration`, and every other
codec-family task remain open. None of the evidence below certifies an entire
module, class, service adapter, or encoding family. Missing APIs, metadata,
annotations, tracebacks and integrations remain blockers, not exceptions.

Read root AGENTS.md; there is no nested AGENTS.md under packages/safe-python.
Preserved unrelated edits, including existing changes to this plan and native
runtime files. No README, CLI, commit, push, release, or build changes were made.

### Implemented and public evidence

- Added native module dictionary storage/type publication in
  `runtime/runtime-module.ts` and `RuntimeTypeRegistry.moduleType()`. Constructor,
  dictionary identity, ordinary mutation, read-only `__dict__`, PEP 562
  `__getattr__` and `__dir__` execute through guest protocols. This is not complete
  ModuleType compatibility: repr, annotation descriptors, precise metadata,
  subclassing edge cases and importlib integration remain unverified/missing.
- Added `runtime/runtime-module-import.ts`, a session-owned module-table importer,
  and wired actual registry/core codec callables into a native `_codecs` module
  in `session.ts`. No host imports, filesystem paths, Python runtime delegation,
  or placeholder codec callables are used. The importer currently has only the
  installed `_codecs` module; package/relative import and importlib/sys.modules
  integration remain unfinished. Imported module `__loader__` and `__spec__`
  are not yet populated with the required importlib objects.
- The `_codecs` bindings share one `RuntimeCodecRegistry` per session. Their
  kernel algorithms were already correct on the exercised cases and were left
  unchanged. This does not initialize the encodings search function or wire
  the registry into native text consumers. In particular, default
  `_codecs.lookup('ascii')` remains unfinished until real standard encoding
  entries/classes are installed; registering custom codecs works.
- Added `src/session-codec-module.test.ts`. Its eight passing tests use the
  default public session/import path, real guest function/class/exception
  machinery, and an explicitly supplied synchronous input service for
  cancellation. They cover native callable/module namespace identity;
  normalized search/cache identity and unregister; per-session registration
  isolation; recursive handlers; mutation of exception.object during __index__;
  tuple/str subtype override avoidance; preserved Unicode exception args;
  all eight standard handlers; rejection of generator callbacks without
  starting their bodies; and terminal cancellation without guest resumption.
  Generator rejection is not evidence of resumable host-callback suspension.
- Two new public assertions are retained as failures: registrations must affect
  str.encode/bytes.decode and str/bytes construction; overridden strict versus
  replace handlers must have the CPython native fast-path distinctions. No
  assertions were weakened, skipped, or marked expected-failure.

sessions. This is not a runtime dependency or a test-suite subprocess call.

### Remaining implementation gates

Complete the real `codecs` and `encodings` modules (including owned aliases,
ascii, latin_1, utf_8 and charmap), real CodecInfo tuple subclass and metadata,
all incremental/stream classes and their state/lifecycle behavior, the standard
search initialization and cache semantics, all remaining `_codecs` functions,
source decoding, text I/O with real supported service adapters, guest traceback
propagation, callback suspension/resumption/cancellation, and exact module/import
metadata and annotations. Full API/type/identity/evaluation-order coverage for
already exposed functions is still required. Existing encoding-family tasks
retain all of their obligations; this bootstrap does not close any of them.

A bounded native text adapter was attempted, then removed because the missing
standard module search initialization changed nine established unknown-encoding
error assertions. The final change preserves those established behaviors;
it does not install a dummy default search function, substitute tuple metadata,
or translate the failing errors to disguise the missing module initialization.
The two new public requirements remain red and keep that work visible.

## Codec text recovery integration — 2026-09-12 (unfinished)

The parent `codec-registry` remains open. This change does not certify any codec
family, public module inventory, source-decoding or text-I/O row as complete.

### Reproduced evidence and implemented behavior

- Read repository `AGENTS.md`, the existing registry/recovery/native text paths,
  session assembly, current pipeline tasks and public codec contract failures.
  Existing workspace edits were preserved; no README, root CLI, commits, pushes
  or releases were changed.
- Before implementation, `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python --
  session-codec-module.test.ts` produced 8 passes and 2 failures: unknown
  `public_text` encoding and failure to honor registered UTF-8 `strict` recovery.
- Added `src/session-codec-text-recovery.test.ts` before implementation. Its
  initial ten cases all failed: two custom encoder conversions, five registered
  strict-handler conversions, mutated decode input/negative resume, retained
  guest failure identity, and service-triggered cancellation.
- `RuntimeExecutionContext` now carries the session's `RuntimeCodecRegistry`
  into each `BuiltinInvocationContext`. Core ASCII/Latin-1/UTF-8 text conversion
  resolves native recovery through that registry. String encoding and bytes
  construction, bytes decoding and string construction share these handlers.
- Extracted `runtime/runtime-core-text-codec.ts` from the existing low-level
  native policy and reused it from `_codecs` bindings and native text factories.
  ASCII/Latin-1 encoding preserves hard-coded strict failure; UTF-8 encoding and
  decoding preserve registry lookup for strict. Other native policy distinctions
  remain in the shared implementation. Each operation owns its lazy handler and
  exception cache through `RuntimeCodecRecovery`; guest object mutation,
  `__index__` validation and cancellation continue through the existing kernels.
- Added two further guest tests for encoder lookup-cache invalidation and
  reentrant handler registration. Final new-file result: 9 passed, 3 failed.
  The three custom encoder/search cases remain executable red requirements.
- External oracle: `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14` reports CPython 3.14.7,
  `[Clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)]`, Unicode 16.0.0. Standalone external
  assertions passed for custom encoder calls/default errors, all five strict
  recovery conversions, negative resume after replacing error.object, retained
  original args, per-operation callback caching, and next-operation registration.
  No Python process is used by the implementation or unit tests.
- External oracle additionally confirms that both custom decoder calls from
  `b'x'.decode('guest')` and `str(b'x', 'guest')` receive `memoryview`. The runtime
  has no published memoryview implementation. Substituting bytes cannot close
  this requirement.

## 2026-09-12 native encoder registry recovery audit

Status: **unfinished**. The original complete codec-registry/module task remains
open, including every earlier owned module/API inventory row and every encoding
family requirement. This repair verifies native encoder recovery only; it does
not certify missing public modules, CodecInfo, incremental classes, streams,

### Reproduction and implementation

Read root AGENTS.md, current registry/recovery/native encoder/decoder code,
package scripts and the preceding ledger before editing. No nested safe-python
AGENTS.md was found. Preserved unrelated edits and did not edit README files,
commit, push or release. No runtime host Python, host eval, ambient capability,
source rewriting, filesystem fixtures or LLM calls were introduced.

Added `src/session-codec-encoder-recovery.test.ts` first. The initial maintained
workspace run produced **150 failures and 18 passes**, 168 tests, 5.46 seconds.
Failures concretely reproduced the missing session error-handler dispatch for
UTF-8-SIG, UTF-16/32 (native/little/big endian) and compiled single-byte encoding.

`runtime/runtime-utf8-encoding.ts` now creates one lazy RuntimeCodecRecovery per
conversion, carrying the original guest string identity and the owning session's
registry. `runtime/runtime-unicode-text-codecs.ts` supplies this callback to wide
Unicode and single-byte table kernels. UTF-8-SIG passes it through
`runtime/utf8-signature.ts` to the existing UTF-8 kernel, including fallback after
surrogateescape's native prefix. Hard-coded failures retain source identity via
the interpreter exception preparation protocol.

Pinned CPython policy distinctions are preserved: wide encoders consult all
registered policies; UTF-8-SIG bypasses replacement registrations for ignore,
replace, backslashreplace, xmlcharrefreplace and surrogatepass, while
surrogateescape first handles escapable surrogates natively. Compiled charmaps
bypass registrations for strict, ignore, replace and xmlcharrefreplace. Other
policies use the registry. UTF-7, escape and Punycode encoders retain their
existing non-recovery behavior; this change does not certify their public APIs.

The final new file contains **217** public PythonSession cases. It tests both
str.encode and bytes(str, encoding, errors), all nine policy names across eight
encoding variants, lazy lookup, original source identity, exception.object
mutation from subtype __index__, tuple/str subtype returns, per-operation handler
and exception caching, reentrant registration, recursive callbacks, guest failure
identity, exact validation exception args (type, ssize_t overflow and bounds),

services. Test services are unit evidence, not final real-adapter certification.

reproduced **4 failed, 18 passed**, 2 files, 4.86 seconds. These are the three

### Implementation and public behavior

`runtime/runtime-wide-codec-functions.ts` creates encode/decode functions for
utf_16, utf_16_le, utf_16_be, utf_32, utf_32_le and utf_32_be, plus both
ex_decode functions. `session.ts` publishes the real functions on its owned
`_codecs` module. Runtime logic stays in the package's runtime implementation.

The bindings use existing pinned wide kernels and the same RuntimeCodecRegistry
and RuntimeCodecRecovery as native text conversion. They validate positional
arity, argument ordering, str subtypes, nullable error names, NUL/surrogate names,
C-int byteorder bounds and final truth conversion. Kernel byteorder uses the
argument's sign; ex_decode preserves the complete supplied C-int value unless
zero requests BOM detection. Native endianness remains explicitly little-endian.

All policy names resolve lazily through the owning registry on actual faults,
including replacements for built-in handlers. Recovery preserves source subtype
identity, per-operation exception caching, mutated decoder input, negative
resume positions, Python tuple/replacement/index validation and guest failures.
Decoder exports are acquired before argument callbacks, copied after callback
mutation, held across decoding and released on success, failure or cancellation.
No host codec, host Unicode classification, ambient capability or runtime Python
process/eval was added.

  `npm run test --workspace=@poe-code/safe-python -- session-wide-codec-api.test.ts runtime-wide-codec-functions.test.ts --reporter=dot`:

The oracle is used only outside unit tests and runtime. Native charmap construction was checked against [CPython 3.14.7 Objects/unicodeobject.c, PyUnicode_BuildEncodingMap and encoding_map_lookup](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.7/Objects/unicodeobject.c#L8151).

Before edits, the unchanged public import/contract gate failed **26/28** tests: seven missing module imports and nineteen public contracts. Four new charmap-build guest programs passed unchanged on the external oracle and failed in PythonSession with `module '_codecs' has no attribute 'charmap_build'`. A fifth unchanged oracle program was added for trie capacity/truncation boundaries.

### Implemented in this continuation

- `runtime/runtime-encoding-map.ts` implements native `_codecs.charmap_build` and EncodingMap trie lookup/size. The first 256 native string code points determine the result. Missing initial NUL, a later NUL, non-BMP mappings and 255 leaf blocks choose the real guest dictionary branch; duplicate mappings retain the last byte. U+FFFE is omitted only by the compact branch. Both branches preserve str-subtype storage without calling virtual length/item methods. The trie is consumed directly by the existing charmap encoder, without exposing a guest subscription protocol.
- `runtime/runtime-type-registry.ts` owns the immutable, non-subclassable, non-instantiable native type; `session.ts` publishes the native function on the actual _codecs module. No module substitute or new ambient service was added.
- `session-charmap-build.test.ts` contains five public guest programs covering dictionary/compact selection, duplicate entries, 253/254/255-leaf capacity, 256-entry truncation, LP64 size values, handler recovery, subtype storage, argument diagnostics, callable descriptor metadata and construction/subclass rejection. All five source literals passed unchanged on the pinned oracle.

These rows establish the tested API behavior, not full EncodingMap introspection compatibility. The pinned oracle also reports EncodingMap.__basicsize__=64, instance.__sizeof__()=64, type.__flags__=4482 before type-cache mutation, instance.__getstate__()=None and pickle rejection; the runtime's general type-size/state/pickle metadata is still absent and remains a blocker.

### Unresolved integration evidence

- `session-codec-module.test.ts` still fails the shared text-consumer registration case with `unknown encoding: public_text`. CPython custom decoders receive a memoryview, including source decoding; substituting bytes would violate the contract. Public memoryview ownership and buffer metadata remain prerequisite work.
- `session-custom-encoder.test.ts` reproduces missing native custom encoder dispatch; `session-codec-text-recovery.test.ts` reproduces unknown registered/CACHE-TEST names. A trial direct registry dispatch was removed: without the real default search bootstrap it changed four already-correct dotted-name errors to the empty-search-path error. No dummy default search function or error normalization was retained.
- `runtime/runtime-core-codec-functions.test.ts` retains three failing traceback assertions for ascii/latin_1/utf_8 rejected replacements. `session-charmap-codec-api.test.ts` retains four failing mapping/handler traceback assertions. The runtime only retains source spans, expressly not CPython instruction positions (`runtime/execution-frame.ts`); `RuntimeExceptionExecution.statements` prepares errors without creating traceback links. Real frame/code/line/instruction propagation must be implemented; no sentinel traceback was introduced.
- Source decoding still invokes native kernels plus an optional explicit decoder and is not wired to the session registry. The pinned oracle probe `compile(b'# coding: source-probe\nignored', 'test.py', 'exec')` calls the custom decoder with one memoryview argument and no explicit errors argument; a non-str result raises the exact decoder TypeError. Text-I/O adapters and synchronous-service suspension remain unfinished.
- The YAML AST audit found codec-registry marked done/done despite these failures. Only its two status scalar ranges were set to open. codec-registry-integration remains open/open.

### Every owned module/API namespace row

The table covers each pinned module's own namespace and every attribute returned by dir() of each class owned by that module, including inherited methods and type metadata. EncodingMap rows inspect type(module.charmap_build(chr(0))); that native type is returned by the factory and is not exported as a module attribute. These additional inherited/type rows expand the initial 486-row own-namespace audit to 1,436 rows.

For each module the probe is `import <module> as module`. For a module row, the expression is `module`; for an API row, the expression is chained `getattr` for each dot-separated API component. Both sides evaluate `type(expression).__name__`. The actual column records the exact type name or `type(error).__name__ + ': ' + str(error)`. Every row used a fresh real PythonSession (1,000,000 steps, 16,000,000 allocated bytes, depth 100, hash seed [1,2]). No builtins or modules were injected. **61/1,436 namespace-type matches, 1,375 blocked/mismatched. A matching row is publication evidence only, never complete callable/metadata verification.**

A separate public-consumer probe found a Punycode recovery bug. After
`_codecs.register_error('strict', handler)`, CPython calls that handler while
decoding the ASCII prefix of `b'\xff-'.decode('punycode')`; safe-python raised
directly without calling it. The same failure occurred through `str(data,

initially produced **10 failures / 2 passes** before the runtime change.

Punycode now decodes its prefix through the existing native ASCII decoder and
the interpreter-owned registry. Its exception-rewriting service enters a real
handled-exception scope, reads `start`, `end`, and `reason` through guest
attribute lookup in Python evaluation order, invokes the real
`UnicodeDecodeError` constructor, and raises the replacement from None.
Attribute and constructor failures retain their original context and are not
prematurely suppressed. Non-Unicode guest failures and fatal cancellation
propagate. No traceback objects, modules, streams, or codec metadata were
fabricated.

The new retained cases cover per-conversion callback caching, reentrant handler
registration, repeated exception identity and initial args, replaced input with
a negative resume position, KeyboardInterrupt identity, UnicodeDecodeError
rewriting, subclass attribute/index order, attribute failures, constructor
validation, preserved ASCII ignore/replace fast paths, unsupported policy
rejection, and cancellation before guest callback resumption. Every case uses
the real public session and native interpreter components. Cancellation uses
the explicit input/output service interfaces in fast in-memory unit tests.

## 2026-09-12 Public registry duplicate-keyword validation — task unfinished

Re-read the repository instructions, registry, native bindings, standard handlers,
session/module initialization, existing public gates and the owned module/API
inventory before editing. The public import and consumer gaps remain reproducible.
The pipeline frontmatter incorrectly marked codec-registry done/done and
codec-registry-integration done/open despite the unresolved requirements. Both
are now open/open. Only those three status scalars were changed using parsed
YAML node ranges; other task statuses, prompts and existing edits were preserved.

### Reproduced bug and implementation

Two distinct str-subtype keyword keys can coexist in a dict with the same native
spelling. `_codecs.encode` and `_codecs.decode` overwrote the first bound value
with the second, then reached registry lookup. CPython rejects the duplicate
through Argument Clinic's unexpected-keyword diagnostic path. This distinction
is observable through equality, truth and string callbacks, their exceptions,
and whether a search callback runs.

`codec-registry-binding-cases.ts` retains 24 unchanged public programs covering
both functions, repeated `obj`/`encoding`/`errors` keys, false/true comparison
results, equality failure and rendering failure. All 24 passed on the external
CPython oracle and failed in the public interpreter before the runtime edit,
each reaching the forbidden search callback (`lookup before keyword validation`).
The native binding now recognizes an already-bound keyword slot and enters its
existing diagnostic path without overwriting the value. There are no new codec
implementations, dispatch exceptions or alternate search functions.

`session-codec-registry-binding.test.ts` also exercises cancellation during
equality, truth and rendering for both functions through explicit input/output
services. All six service scenarios terminate before guest recovery and leave
the session cancelled. These are fast in-memory service tests, not proof of
asynchronous suspension or completed real stream-adapter compatibility.

### Reproduction and change

The imported `_codecs.register` search path was bypassed by `str.encode`,
`str.encode(source, ...)`, `bytes(source, encoding)` and
`bytes.__new__(bytes, source, encoding)`. Each raised `LookupError: unknown

had an optional injected fallback but never used the invocation's registry for
an otherwise unknown encoding.

the invocation-owned registry when its search path is populated. The registry's
metered `hasSearchFunctions` accessor exposes actual search-path availability;
no callback or module is synthesized. Explicit injected fallback precedence,
existing native codec behavior, empty-search-path unknown-encoding diagnostics,
and ordinary result validation are preserved. Default `encodings` search-path
initialization remains unimplemented and required under

integration or compatibility when default search initialization is required.
